nodes.name: ATLAS Universal MCP Server for Logistics
nodes.description: Fork of Cargofy's ATLAS (AI Transport Logistics Agent Standard): a self-hosted Node MCP server that indexes a logistics company's shipments, carriers, lanes, rates, documents, tracking events and disruption issues into SQLite/PostgreSQL and exposes them to AI agents over MCP (stdio and HTTP/SSE) plus a REST API and web UI. In the Notations Universe it is the candidate logistics-context provider for the physical-economy layer: agents ask it questions, raw operational data never leaves the perimeter. It must never become the canonical world state; it is a read-mostly context index with operator-gated ingestion (seed, file import, AI extraction, connector sync, knowledge base edits).

capabilities.label: MCP: list enabled data models
capabilities.description: Lists all enabled ATLAS data models (shipments, carriers, lanes, rates, documents, tracking_events, service_levels and opt-in extensions) with record counts. Agents call it before querying.

capabilities.label: MCP: get model schema
capabilities.description: Returns the JSON Schema and description for one ATLAS data model (models/*.json, published under https://atlasmcp.org/models/<model>/v1).

capabilities.label: MCP: list carriers
capabilities.description: Lists all indexed carriers with id, name, country, type (trucking, shipping_line, airline, rail, freight_broker, 3pl) and rating.

capabilities.label: MCP: list lanes
capabilities.description: Lists indexed origin-to-destination lanes with mode and average transit days for which rate data exists.

capabilities.label: MCP: list document types
capabilities.description: Lists logistics document types indexed (BOL, CMR, AWB, invoice, customs, POD, packing list, certificate of origin, dangerous goods) with counts.

capabilities.label: MCP: data freshness and connector health
capabilities.description: Returns per-table record counts and last sync timestamps plus connector runner statistics (runs, last_run, interval).

capabilities.label: MCP: query any model with filters
capabilities.description: Generic query over any enabled model by name with field-equality filters and limit (max 200). Used for extension models such as tenders, assets, issues, load_listings.

capabilities.label: MCP: natural-language search
capabilities.description: Keyword/natural-language search across all indexed logistics data (shipments, carriers, lanes) returning ranked results and a context block. v0.1 uses keyword matching; vector search is on the roadmap.

capabilities.label: MCP: get shipment by id
capabilities.description: Returns full details of one shipment: mode, status, origin/destination, carrier, cargo, planned/actual dates, financials.

capabilities.label: MCP: list shipments
capabilities.description: Lists shipments filtered by status (pending, in_transit, customs, delivered, exception, cancelled), mode (road, ocean, air, rail, multimodal) and date range.

capabilities.label: MCP: shipment tracking timeline
capabilities.description: Returns the tracking event timeline (pickup, transit, delivery, exception scans with location and optional lat/lon) for one shipment, optionally exceptions only.

capabilities.label: MCP: unsigned documents for a shipment
capabilities.description: Returns documents attached to a shipment that are still pending signature.

capabilities.label: MCP: shipment closure checklist
capabilities.description: Computes what is still needed to close a shipment (POD, signatures, review) and returns it as a checklist for review; does not change state.

capabilities.label: MCP: search carriers
capabilities.description: Searches carriers by ISO country, type, minimum rating or free text.

capabilities.label: MCP: shipments handled by a carrier
capabilities.description: Lists all shipments handled by a given carrier id with carrier name.

capabilities.label: MCP: freight rate history
capabilities.description: Retrieves freight rate history for a lane (ISO origin/destination), carrier and mode over a date range; at least one of origin, destination or carrier_id is required.

capabilities.label: MCP: list logistics documents
capabilities.description: Lists logistics documents filtered by shipment id or document type.

capabilities.label: MCP: SLA violations
capabilities.description: Returns shipments that exceeded their service-level planned transit time, filterable by mode, origin/destination country and sync time. Core exception-management observation.

capabilities.label: MCP: idle assets
capabilities.description: Returns assets (trucks/vehicles, extension model) that appear stationary with engine running beyond an idle-minutes threshold.

capabilities.label: MCP: tracking anomalies
capabilities.description: Returns all tracking events flagged as exceptions since a timestamp.

capabilities.label: MCP: active disruption issues
capabilities.description: Returns unresolved operational disruption issues (carrier no-show, cargo not ready, mechanical failure, customs hold, border closure, tender withdrawal and 20+ standard types) filterable by type, severity and requires_replanning.

capabilities.label: MCP stdio transport
capabilities.description: Full 21-tool MCP server over stdio for Claude Desktop / CLI clients (node src/index.js; docker run cargofy/atlas node src/index.js). README claims 35 tools; code registers 21.

capabilities.label: MCP HTTP/SSE transport
capabilities.description: Remote MCP: GET /mcp opens an SSE session (bearer-token auth from config auth.tokens), POST /mcp/message?sessionId= carries client messages. This transport registers a 12-tool subset (discovery, shipments, carriers, rates, documents, query).

capabilities.label: Health report
capabilities.description: GET /api/health returns overall status (healthy/degraded), version, uptime, per-table record counts and per-connector health (ok/starting/error/stale). Used by the Docker HEALTHCHECK.

capabilities.label: Server status and setup status
capabilities.description: GET /api/status and GET /api/setup/status return instance name, config source, whether AI/auth are configured and whether the setup wizard is needed.

capabilities.label: REST: read table rows
capabilities.description: GET /api/data/{shipments|carriers|routes|rates|documents|events}?limit&search returns raw rows from the local store; POST /api/query dispatches a named read tool (query, get_shipment, search_carriers, get_rate_history, list_documents) for the Explorer/Playground UI.

capabilities.label: REST: list connectors
capabilities.description: GET /api/connectors lists configured data-source connectors (rest_api, filesystem, ai_extract) with sync interval and stats.

capabilities.label: REST: trigger connector sync
capabilities.description: POST /api/connectors/{id}/sync runs a connector immediately, pulling from the external TMS/ERP/rate API and upserting records into the local store.

capabilities.label: REST: seed database
capabilities.description: POST /api/import/seed loads the bundled seed/ dataset (synthetic shipments, carriers, lanes, rates, documents, parties, tracking events, service levels, tenders, assets, issues) into the store.

capabilities.label: REST: import data files
capabilities.description: POST /api/import/file and POST /api/import/folder ingest JSON, CSV or XLSX rows mapped by filename to an entity; POST /api/import/ai runs AI entity extraction over an uploaded document (PDF, CSV, XLSX, email) and writes extracted shipments/carriers/rates/documents.

capabilities.label: REST: chat with tools
capabilities.description: POST /api/chat runs a conversational LLM turn (Claude, OpenAI or Ollama via role routing) that can call ATLAS read tools; GET /api/ai/models and /api/ai/stats expose configured models and usage.

capabilities.label: REST: read/write config
capabilities.description: GET /api/config reads the YAML config (tokens redacted by the UI); POST /api/config writes config.yml; POST /api/admin/reload hot-reloads; POST /api/setup/save and /api/setup/test-ai back the first-run wizard.

capabilities.label: REST: prune old records
capabilities.description: POST /api/admin/prune deletes records older than storage.retention_days (default 90) and expired rates.

capabilities.label: REST: knowledge base files
capabilities.description: GET /api/kb/tree and GET /api/kb/file read the markdown enterprise knowledge base; POST/DELETE /api/kb/file and POST /api/kb/folder edit it; POST /api/knowledge/enrich asks the LLM to append facts and flag contradictions from extractions.

capabilities.label: REST: plugin modules
capabilities.description: GET /api/modules lists file-watch, knowledge-enricher and google-drive modules with status; POST /api/modules/{id}/enable|disable|sync toggles them or forces a run (google-drive pulls files from Drive and runs AI analysis).

capabilities.label: Outbound webhooks
capabilities.description: Wire contract: when configured in config.yml, ATLAS POSTs JSON {event, timestamp, atlas_version, payload} with an HMAC-SHA256 X-Atlas-Signature header for sla_violation, sync_error, new_exception, new_issue and sync_complete events; fire-and-forget with one retry.

capabilities.label: CLI: atlas init/validate/seed/status/start
capabilities.description: bin/atlas.js: init writes a config.yml interactively, validate checks it, seed loads JSON/CSV/XLSX files from a folder, status prints record counts and sync times, start launches the HTTP server.

capabilities.label: ATLAS data model schemas
capabilities.description: JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) contracts for shipment, carrier, route, document, rate and event, validated with AJV (npm run validate-models). The wire contract other logistics systems map onto.

capabilities.label: Web UI
capabilities.description: Single-page web UI on port 3000: Dashboard, Explorer, Chat, Playground, Knowledge Base, Import, Connectors, Modules, Settings and Setup Wizard.

nodes.name: BIM State Transformer Engine (GAT)
nodes.description: Portable, decision-focused computational state runtime for BIM. Its GAT (Gaussian Architectural Transformer) core compiles IFC design intent into an architectural IR and a joint Gaussian belief (mu, Sigma), absorbs calibrated physical evidence (scan PLY registration, material certificates) by Bayesian conditioning, propagates consequences through analytic Jacobians, verifies invariants with rollback, and records every accepted or rejected transition in a hash-chained execution ledger. It is the built-environment world model of the universe: one addressable computational state with explicit IFC, JSON-snapshot and optionally Ed25519-signed OpenUSD carriers, a read-only gat-headless JSON boundary for hosts (Blender, CI), an SP1 zero-knowledge guest that attests one bounded ANSI/AISC 360-22 beam calculation, and a Blender 4.2 sidebar. It must never authorize a physical intervention, never let a probabilistic assessment become an approval, never let a USD view or a splat become truth without passing the typed measurement boundary, and is not an HTTP service (pure Python + numpy, optional usd-core).

capabilities.label: Fail-closed IFC compatibility audit
capabilities.description: `gat audit model.ifc [--text|--html|--compact] [-o path]` (alias `gat-ifc-audit`) inventories an IFC STEP file without mutating or partially importing it: schema, unit context, missing quantities, geometry fallbacks, placement limits, lower/compile/verify outcome, bound to the input bytes. Exit 0 pipeline-ready, 2 unsupported content, 3 I/O. Never authorizes a decision.

capabilities.label: Probabilistic clash report
capabilities.description: `gat check model.ifc [--proposed duct.json] [--max-clearance 0.5] [--fail-above 0.5] [--json]` scores every solid element pair under the joint belief: clearance, sigma via the relative Jacobian, P(clash)=Phi(-c/sigma), overlap mass, chi-square separation significance and witness axes; a proposed oriented box ({origin, extents, angle_deg, position_sigma}) is scored against all existing elements. Exit 1 when any P(clash) reaches the threshold.

capabilities.label: Invariants and compliance under uncertainty
capabilities.description: `gat verify model.ifc [--json]` runs the full invariant registry plus every compliance rule as a margin with mean and sigma under the joint belief (P(satisfied)=Phi(mu/sigma), PASS/MARGINAL/FAIL). Exit 0 when all pass, 1 on findings, 2 on input errors.

capabilities.label: State census, sensitivities and variance attribution
capabilities.description: `gat inspect model.ifc [--var Entity-Name.Quantity] [--top N] [--json]` prints the entity census, raw/derived variable counts, state digest and sampled spread; with --var it returns mean +- sigma, exact d(target)/d(raw) sensitivities and a variance attribution that sums to one.

capabilities.label: 3DGS splat export with belief-sampled variations
capabilities.description: `gat splats model.ifc out/ [--variations N] [--seed S] [--spacing 0.75]` writes building.ply in the standard 3D Gaussian Splatting PLY layout (positions, quaternions, log-scales, SH DC colour by semantic class) loadable in stock 3DGS viewers, plus N sampled realizations of N(mu, Sigma) with a manifest.json recording each sample's dimensions and verification status. Writes files to a caller-chosen directory; never mutates the model.

capabilities.label: Monte-Carlo invariant checking over belief realizations
capabilities.description: `gat sample model.ifc [--n 500] [--seed 0] [--json]` samples realizations of the joint belief and reports pass rate and per-invariant violation rates; the test suite asserts these agree with the analytic delta-method clash scores within Monte-Carlo error.

capabilities.label: Render a gat-headless response for humans
capabilities.description: `gat report response.json|- [--html] [-o out]` renders any gat-headless-response-v1 (summary, acceptance disposition, beam-assurance verdict change, change-impact preview, or error) as terminal text or a self-contained script-free HTML page sharing one signal palette with the Blender panel. Exit 0 rendered, 1 rendered error response, 2 invalid input, 3 I/O.

capabilities.label: Render a chain-verified execution-ledger timeline
capabilities.description: `gat ledger ledger.json [--html] [-o out]` decodes a gat-execution-ledger v1 file, verifies the hash chain and renders accepted/rejected transitions, assessments, policies, approvals and external actions as a timeline. Exit 2 on an invalid or tampered chain.

capabilities.label: Offline 3D viewer of belief and sampled as-builts
capabilities.description: `gat view model.ifc -o viewer.html [--variations N] [--seed S] [--spacing]` writes a single self-contained HTML page with the derived scene JSON embedded, showing the nominal belief and sampled realizations without any server.

capabilities.label: gat-headless: summary of a loaded authoritative state
capabilities.description: `gat-headless request.json [-o response.json] [--trusted-key KEY_ID=PATH]` with operation `summary` returns source, entity/relationship/constraint counts, raw/derived variable counts, invariant pass/warn/fail counts and the world digest for a state of kind ifc | snapshot | openusd | usd. Deterministic command handler, not a server; stdin `-` supported. Error responses carry {type, message} and exit 2.

capabilities.label: gat-headless: fail-closed acceptance case disposition
capabilities.description: Operation `acceptance` evaluates an AcceptanceCase (workflow AS_BUILT_CLEARANCE | OPENING_VERIFICATION | design-change; checks of kind clearance, minimum, difference bound to one world digest) under the gat-safe-acceptance-v1 policy and returns exactly one disposition: ACCEPT, REJECT or REQUEST_EVIDENCE. Evidence receipts must resolve to a verified ObserveLinearized transition in the ledger carried in an OpenUSD file whose Ed25519 signature verifies against a deployment-configured trusted key. ACCEPT is a recommendation, not an ApprovalRecord.

capabilities.label: gat-headless: evidence-driven ANSI/AISC 360-22 beam assurance
capabilities.description: Operation `beam_assurance` loads a beam state and a strict versioned material certificate, conditions an ephemeral session (Gaussian update of fy), executes the validated ansi-aisc-360-22-f2-1-lrfd-v1 chain in memory and returns prior/revised capacity distributions, SATISFIED/VIOLATED/UNRESOLVED verdict change, evidence identity, transition/assessment ledger hashes, code/oracle identities and `may_authorize: false`. Never edits the source IFC or certificate.

capabilities.label: gat-headless: non-mutating design-change / RFI impact preview
capabilities.description: Operation `change_impact` previews a set_parameter, shift_parameter or scale_parameter change through the exact apply -> propagate -> verify pipeline and returns candidate impacts and invariant failures without committing; the authoritative world is unchanged.

capabilities.label: Python API: load a session from IFC, snapshot, OpenUSD or USDA
capabilities.description: `GatSession.load_ifc(path)`, `load_snapshot(path)`, `load_openusd(path, trusted_public_keys=, require_signature=)` and `load_usd(path)` compile a source into IR -> Gaussian belief and run the full invariant registry. OpenUSD carriers v1/v2/v3 are accepted under bounded read budgets; the ledger head must match the restored world; signature verification fails closed when required.

capabilities.label: Python API: commit a verified transformation to the belief
capabilities.description: `session.run(op, provenance=)` applies a closed operator (SetParameter/ShiftParameter/ScaleParameter do-interventions, ObserveQuantity/ObserveLinearized Gaussian conditioning, EvolveLinearGaussian process step), re-propagates derived state incrementally, runs every invariant, and either commits or rolls back with digest proof; both outcomes are appended to the session's hash-chained gat-execution-ledger. This is the only path by which canonical belief changes.

capabilities.label: Python API: record assessments, policies, approvals and external actions
capabilities.description: `session.record_assessment`, `record_policy`, `record_approval`, `record_external_action` append typed, state-bound causal events (gat/causal.py) that must preserve the world digest; approval and external-action ids follow explicit lifecycles and stale assessments fail closed. Names such as `authority` are not identity proofs.

capabilities.label: Python API: export IFC, JSON, snapshot, ledger, USDA and OpenUSD carriers
capabilities.description: `export_ifc` round-trips posterior means and sigmas in the source unit convention; `export_json` writes the compact dashboard projection; `export_snapshot` writes GatStateSnapshot v1 (closed IR, raw order, dense covariance, integrity digest); `export_ledger` writes the ledger; `export_usd` the zero-dependency USDA proof; `export_openusd(path, signing_key=)` the native carrier v3 with /State authoritative, /View derived, and an optional Ed25519 signature over belief, trace and ledger head.

capabilities.label: Python API: replay and verify an execution ledger
capabilities.description: `read_ledger(path)` and `replay_ledger(checkpoint_world, ledger)` regenerate every accepted commit and rejected attempt from a trusted checkpoint and must reproduce the exact dense joint belief and digests; bounded parsing detects edits, deletion and reordering. An unsigned chain does not establish publisher identity.

capabilities.label: Python API: decision assessment and active-inference evidence planning
capabilities.description: `assess_decision(world, MinimumDecision)` returns SATISFIED/VIOLATED/UNRESOLVED at a required confidence; `plan_decision_evidence(world, decision, [ObservationCandidate])` ranks scalar observations by a one-step expected-free-energy proxy (pragmatic risk + cost in nats - mutual information). Selecting an action never mutates state; only a later real reading conditions the belief.

capabilities.label: Python API: register an external scan PLY and quarantine evidence
capabilities.description: `load_ply_points(path)` reads ASCII or binary-little-endian PLY vertices (including mesh vertices such as Geometry-Grounded-Gaussian-Splatting's recon_post.ply); `ScanRegistrar(derive_scene(world)).register(points)` runs robust GMM scan-to-BIM registration (8 starts, EM, Gauss-Newton yaw) and `registrar.evidence(points, registration)` yields a per-element evidence report bound to the scan SHA-256 and scene version. Evidence stops before conditioning BIM dimensions.

capabilities.label: Python API: as-built MEP clearance assurance and calibrated scan likelihood
capabilities.description: `assess_clearance(scene, ClearanceDecision)` evaluates a proposed oriented box against every solid element with dependence-safe bounds max(Pi) <= P(any) <= min(1, sum Pi); `plan_clearance_evidence` recommends a calibrated element measurement or targeted rescan; `adapt_clearance_likelihood` turns accepted scan evidence plus an independent survey/SLAM pose covariance into a belief-bound ObserveLinearized that can enter session.run after provenance, support, alignment, coverage, pose-agreement and innovation gates.

capabilities.label: Python API: sensitivities, variance attribution, Lyapunov stability, configuration digest
capabilities.description: `sensitivities_of(world, var)`, `variance_attribution(world, var)`, `gat.engine.stability.analyze(world, ops)` (contracting/marginal/amplifying with an uncertainty-energy trace) and `configuration_digest(world)` (identity modulo relabeling, rigid motion and re-encoding); `forecast_process(world, EvolveLinearGaussian, steps)` rolls a calibrated linear-Gaussian process forward without mutation.

capabilities.label: Python API: proof-carrying computation manifest binding and verification
capabilities.description: `create_computation_proof_manifest(ledger, event_seq=, numeric_contract=, ... proof_artifact=)` packages one accepted ledger transition as a gat-computation-proof-manifest v1 binding prior/result worlds, operation, verification, ledger head, program and verifying-key digests, numerical contract and proof bytes; `verify_computation_proof_manifest(manifest, ledger, proof_bytes, verifier=)` checks the binding and delegates to a host-supplied backend verifier. Binding alone is not proof verification.

capabilities.label: SP1 zero-knowledge guest: execute, prove, verify the bounded beam claim
capabilities.description: Rust host `gat-sp1-beam {execute|prove|verify} --request r.json [--proof p --receipt rc]` runs the pinned SP1 v6.5.0 (circuit v6.1.0) RISC-V guest that commits domain, public-statement digest, fixed-computation digest, nominal and available capacity (milli-N*mm), demand and PASS/FAIL for the checked fixed-point F2-1 calculation. `python -m gat.demo.beam_sp1 out --executable <host>` generates a core proof, verifies it and binds it into the manifest via `sp1_beam_subprocess_verifier`. Proves computation integrity only, never certificate truth, Gaussian correctness, code applicability or safety.

capabilities.label: Wire contract: SP1 beam request and receipt JSON
capabilities.description: `read_sp1_beam_request`/`write_sp1_beam_request` and `read_sp1_beam_receipt` define the strict request (format, schema_version, sp1_version, sp1_circuit_version, transition_event_seq, public_statement_digest, numeric_contract beam-milli-mpa-mm3-milli-nmm-v1, claim, expected_public_values_hex) and receipt (program, verifying-key, proof, statement and result commitments) shared byte-for-byte between Python and Rust with a checked known vector.

capabilities.label: Wire contract: strict versioned material certificate
capabilities.description: `read_material_certificate(path)` accepts a MEASURED certificate preserving issuer, batch, specimen, calibration and exact source identity (demo fixture gat/demo/material_certificate.json: fy 325 +- 2 MPa). Signature, revocation and issuer trust are explicitly unverified.

capabilities.label: Reference experiment: complete evidence-to-verification beam chain
capabilities.description: `python -m gat.demo.beam_assurance out/beam` runs IfcBeam -> canonical state -> typed certificate -> Gaussian conditioning -> bending capacity -> verdict -> state-bound assessment -> replay/snapshot -> checked fixed-point claim, writing IFC, snapshot, ledger, summary and SP1 proof request to out_dir. Self-asserting; the sibling demos (`python -m gat.demo`, `.geometry`, `.active_inference`, `.portability`, `.openusd_portability`, `.beam_openusd_portability`, `.temporal_process`, `.workflow`, `.usd`, `.ledger_replay`, `.incremental_scale`) are the same kind of executable proof.

capabilities.label: Fetch and verify the commit-pinned public IFC validation corpus
capabilities.description: `python validation/fetch_ifc_corpus.py <dir> [--include-large]` downloads models declared in validation/ifc-corpus-v1.json (buildingSMART sample files, Medical-Dental Clinic 19 MB, optional 65 MB Schependomlaan) from pinned GitHub commits and refuses any size or sha256 mismatch; tests.test_public_ifc_corpus then checks measured audit baselines (GAT_IFC_VALIDATION_ROOT).

capabilities.label: Blender 4.2+ GAT Evidence and Assurance sidebar
capabilities.description: Extension `gat_assurance` v0.2.0 (integrations/blender) loads a completed gat-headless `acceptance` or `beam_assurance` response, shows disposition, next evidence request or capacity/verdict change with method and oracle identity, and colours matching Blender/Bonsai objects by name or `gat_entity_name` property. Read-only: no IFC edits, no transformations, no probabilities recomputed; requests local file access only. Build: `blender --command extension build --source-dir integrations/blender/gat_assurance`.

nodes.name: Notations Ecosystem Control Plane
nodes.description: The private coordination backend of the Notations Universe: an append-only, SHA-256 hash-linked and Ed25519-signed journal of node registrations, relations, health observations, security posture and capability requests. Credentials resolve to principals whose roles decide what they may do and which actor identity they may record, so the audit trail is authenticated rather than self-asserted. It records intent and operator approval but never stores provider credentials, key material, vulnerability detail or network topology, and never dispatches an external call.

capabilities.label: Read the ecosystem snapshot
capabilities.description: GET /v1/snapshot: current nodes (with derived health), relations, coordination records, revision and event cursor.

capabilities.label: Read events after a cursor
capabilities.description: GET /v1/events?after=<eventCursor>&limit=<n>: append-only records after a known cursor, paginated with a server-side cap; 409 CURSOR_UNKNOWN means refresh the snapshot.

capabilities.label: Liveness and journal summary
capabilities.description: GET /health (unauthenticated): liveness and uptime only. It deliberately discloses no revision and no node count, so an anonymous caller learns nothing about history.

capabilities.label: Register or revise a node
capabilities.description: POST /v1/commands action=register_node with expectedRevision. Declares a node's kind, capabilities (observe/propose/execute), bounded metadata and optional location.

capabilities.label: Declare a relation between nodes
capabilities.description: POST /v1/commands action=declare_relation: supplies_context_to, coordinates, visualizes, governs or depends_on between two registered nodes.

capabilities.label: Record a health observation
capabilities.description: POST /v1/commands action=record_observation from an operator, health check or webhook; derives the node's health in the snapshot.

capabilities.label: Request a capability of another node
capabilities.description: POST /v1/commands action=request_capability: a reasoning engine or dock states intent to use a target capability in its declared mode; execute intents become approval_required and stay dispatch=not_dispatched.

capabilities.label: Approve or reject a coordination request
capabilities.description: POST /v1/commands action=resolve_coordination by an operator. Separation of duties: the approving actor may not be the actor that proposed the intent. Approval is not execution: the record stays not_dispatched.

capabilities.label: Read the control plane's own security posture
capabilities.description: GET /v1/security/status: identity binding, the authorization model, transport state, key lifecycle, journal integrity and abuse counters. Requires the operator or admin role. Names no credential, key, address or journal content.

capabilities.label: Record a security posture attestation
capabilities.description: POST /v1/commands action=record_security_posture: up to 12 signals across identity, authorization, encryption, key lifecycle, dependency risk, exposure, audit integrity, backup, incident and control-plane integrity. Carries states, coverage fractions and severity counts only.

capabilities.label: Issue a principal credential
capabilities.description: CLI: mints an ncp.<keyId>.<secret> credential bound to a principal, its roles, the actor identities it may claim and optionally the nodes it may act for. The secret is printed once; only a SHA-256 digest is stored.

capabilities.label: Rotate the journal signing key
capabilities.description: CLI: generates a new Ed25519 signing key, retires the previous one and records the journal length from which the new key is expected. Records signed by the retired key keep verifying.

nodes.name: Data Acquisition Channel (DAQ / Data Acquisition Fabric)
nodes.description: The acquisition entry of the Notations scientific substrate. Adapters for permitted external sources (arXiv, SEC EDGAR, USGS earthquakes, NOAA water levels, local and GPC datasets) feed the vendored Scientific Transformer Engine's SCOUT admission contract, persisting content-addressed evidence, execution records and quarantine into a durable pool behind a source catalog, repeatable plans and checkpoints. A neutral intent/bridge seam turns scientific information gaps into acquisition plans, and 52 architecture invariants plus content-addressed exchange artifacts are shared with the Scientific Compute Layer. It also hosts Notation Physical Commerce (commerce/): an append-only freight ledger, CanadaBuys tender ingest, landed cost, carrier vetting and an operator CLI, placed here while Sea Dog Terminal is frozen. Kind is api, not information_library: no corpus is committed (every evidence pool is built per run against a local root) and the surface is Python contracts plus CLIs; no HTTP or MCP server exists. It must never write canonical state directly (STE promotes), never let an interpretation become its own evidence, and never let an agent bind the firm.

capabilities.label: List registered acquisition sources
capabilities.description: `python -m daf.catalog.cli <root> list-sources` prints every persisted SourceDefinition (source_id, name, domain, adapter_id, enabled) from `<root>/sources/*.json`. `inspect-source <source_id>` prints one definition in full. Read-only over operator-declared catalog state.

capabilities.label: List and inspect repeatable acquisition plans
capabilities.description: `list-plans` prints every persisted AcquisitionPlan (plan_id, source_id, enabled, schedule) from `<root>/plans/`; `inspect-plan <plan_id>` prints one. Plans are declarative {plan_id, source_id, parameters, enabled, schedule, mode snapshot|incremental, interval_seconds}; nothing here executes them.

capabilities.label: Validate an acquisition plan without running it
capabilities.description: `validate-plan <plan_id>` runs `daf.catalog.plan.validate_plan` and prints PlanValidationIssue codes (unknown/disabled source, unknown adapter, disabled plan, missing required parameters, INVALID_MODE, incremental mode on a source that does not declare it). Exit 1 on any issue. Structural, non-raising, no network.

capabilities.label: Execute an acquisition plan (checkpoint-aware ingest)
capabilities.description: `execute-plan <plan_id> <requested_at>` restores the DurablePool from `<root>/evidence`, runs `daf.scheduling.runner.execute_plan` through the unmodified SCOUT admission path, prints outcome (acquired|duplicate|source_unavailable|adapter_failure|extraction_failure|persistence_failure) and each artifact_id/version_id/is_new, and advances the plan checkpoint only on acquired/duplicate. Live network for arxiv, edgar-daily-index, usgs-earthquakes and noaa-water-level bindings. At-least-once, deduplicated by content address.

capabilities.label: Register a source definition or acquisition plan (Python API)
capabilities.description: `SourceCatalog(root).register(SourceDefinition)` and `PlanCatalog(root).register(AcquisitionPlan)` persist operator configuration as last-write-wins JSON per id (deliberately not content-addressed: catalog entries are mutable configuration, never evidence). Registration is programmatic only; there is no CLI verb, mirroring `daf.orchestration.bindings` as the single place adapters are wired.

capabilities.label: Run one acquisition request through the orchestrator
capabilities.description: `AcquisitionOrchestrator(sources, adapters, pool).run(AcquisitionRequest{source_id, parameters, requested_at}) -> AcquisitionResult{source_id, outcome, artifacts, admission_failures, error}`. Selects the source, builds its adapter, fetches, then admits via the vendored `scout.pipeline.run_scout`; it never calls a pool mutator or `evidence.admission` directly (AST-verified). Failures are classified by stage and reported, never raised. Callers in a fresh process must use `DurablePool.restore` for duplicate detection.

capabilities.label: Run every plan that is due (scheduler interface, not a daemon)
capabilities.description: `is_due(plan, checkpoints, now)`, `due_plans(plans, checkpoints, now)` and `run_due_plans(...)` are pure functions of (plan.interval_seconds, checkpoint.updated_at, now) that call `execute_plan` for each due plan and return the AcquisitionResults. Nothing reads the clock; the caller supplies `now`. Deterministic and testable; no background process exists.

capabilities.label: Execute a plan with a durable execution record and quarantine
capabilities.description: `execute_plan_recorded(...) -> RecordedExecution(result, execution, quarantine)`: mints a stable operation_id from the plan and an execution_id before anything runs, executes the unmodified Phase-E path, then persists an ExecutionRecord (two-hash identity: id over {operation_id, runtime_id, started_at}, content_digest over everything else) to `<root>/executions/` and one QuarantineRecord per refused admission to `<root>/quarantine/`. Records are never evidence and never change the pool fingerprint.

capabilities.label: Ingest rejection metrics and unclassified backlog
capabilities.description: `rejection_metrics`, `unclassified_backlog` and `ingest_report` compute per-invariant rejection rates per ingest run and the backlog of evidence with no class, purely over existing execution/quarantine/class records. Derived views with no identity and no persistence, so they cannot drift from what they describe. Raises QuarantineAccountingError if the buckets do not conserve.

capabilities.label: Read the durable evidence pool
capabilities.description: `DurablePool.restore(FilesystemEvidenceStore(root))` / `load_pool(store)` expose the vendored EvidencePool read surface (get_*/has_*/all_*/fingerprint/fingerprint_history) over content-addressed JSON files, with lazy hydration so hot-path lookups are O(1) file reads. `ClassifiedPool` additionally returns the evidence class assigned at ingest (class_assigned_at_ingest invariant). Reads only; every write path is the SCOUT pipeline.

capabilities.label: Artifact / version / content identity queries
capabilities.description: `ArtifactStore(store)` answers `exists(artifact_id, version_id)`, `get`, `list_versions(artifact_id)`, `find_by_content_hash`, `list_source_artifacts(source_id)`; `daf.catalog.history.known_versions/has_ever_been_acquired` derive acquisition history from it. artifact_id = hash(source_id, locator) is a derived, non-authoritative grouping key; version_id is the real Document.id; content_hash is the raw bytes alone.

capabilities.label: SQLite metadata index over the evidence store
capabilities.description: `MetadataIndex(path)` stores only ids and the columns real queries need (artifact_id, source_id, content_hash, retrieved_at, locator) and answers list_versions, find_by_content_hash, list_source_artifacts, locator_for_document, all_ids(category), is_empty; `rebuild(store)` re-derives it from the filesystem store, which remains the sole authority for what evidence exists. Never raw content.

capabilities.label: Acquire arXiv papers (Atom API, snapshot-by-id)
capabilities.description: `ArxivSourceAdapter` (adapter_id `arxiv`) issues one HTTPS GET to export.arxiv.org/api/query?id_list=... and emits one RawDocument per Atom <entry> holding the raw substring byte-identical to what arXiv sent (source_kind paper, retrieval_method http:arxiv_api_v1, retrieved_at caller-supplied). `ArxivExtractor` yields paper and author referents and relations. Assigns no identity of its own; fetch_bytes is injectable for tests.

capabilities.label: Acquire SEC EDGAR daily index files (incremental)
capabilities.description: `EdgarDailyIndexSourceAdapter` (adapter_id `edgar-daily-index`) lists sec.gov/Archives/edgar/daily-index/<year>/<qtr>/index.json and fetches at most max_dates_per_fetch (default 5) daily .idx files newer than the checkpoint position, under a declared EDGAR_USER_AGENT per SEC fair-access policy, retrying only 429/5xx at most twice. Volume per call is bounded; there is deliberately NO request-rate ceiling (recorded as not_enforced in architecture/daq_agent_instruments.yaml). Extractor: text:edgar_daily_index_v1.

capabilities.label: Acquire USGS earthquake events (FDSN event service, incremental)
capabilities.description: `UsgsEarthquakesSourceAdapter` (adapter_id `usgs-earthquakes`) queries earthquake.usgs.gov/fdsnws/event/1/query and event detail documents, advancing an epoch-ms position per run. The extractor carries the source's own method provenance and quantity semantics (magnitude type, units) into Observation content rather than inventing them.

capabilities.label: Acquire NOAA CO-OPS water-level series (window and per-reading)
capabilities.description: `NoaaWaterLevelSourceAdapter` (adapter_ids `noaa-water-level` and `noaa-water-level-measurements`) fetches api.tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov datagetter windows for a station/datum/unit and emits either one window document or one Observation per reading with scalar value, measurement_time, unit, sigma (uncertainty_kind stated) and conditions={datum}. The only live external scientific modality supplied today. Known gaps: time_zone=gmt is dropped; ordering and sampling interval are not represented; method provenance is MISSING, so readings stay inadmissible for canonical assertion.

capabilities.label: Acquire local JSON datasets (snapshot, incremental cursor, graph)
capabilities.description: Three file-based adapters through the same SourceAdapter Protocol: `local-dataset` reads a whole JSON file (extractor emits zero entities by design); `incremental-dataset` returns records whose caller-authored integer `sequence` exceeds the checkpoint position; `graph-dataset` passes structured records with declared property/subject fields through verbatim. Deterministic, no network; they prove the orchestrator generalises across acquisition shapes.

capabilities.label: Acquire GPC/SEC chromatography reports and physico-chemical study fixtures
capabilities.description: `GpcReportSourceAdapter` emits one RawDocument per RUN (run identity on the locator, never in content) from a JSON report, and `GpcSummaryExportSourceAdapter` reads vendor CSV-with-header exports where replicates are rows. Both require caller-declared `data_provenance`, `sample_kind`, `method`, `unit` marked `acquisition_declared`, refuse when missing, and carry conditions verbatim. Anchors: EPA P-22-0051 Waters Empower report, R190048 Impact export, WIL 505902 OECD 105 study. Local files only; the polymer vertical's first ingest path.

capabilities.label: EDGAR_SCOUT agent contract and candidate-filing schema validation
capabilities.description: The generated contract `docs/generated/AGENT_EDGAR_SCOUT.md` authorises an executing model to PROPOSE which SEC filings are worth acquiring (rank, estimate relevance in [0,1], decline with a query_gap) and forbids network requests, invented identifiers, and writing state. `daf.agents.candidate_filing.validate(payload, schema)` mechanically refuses output violating `architecture/schemas/candidate_filing.schema.json`, and refuses any schema keyword it does not implement.

capabilities.label: Diagnose the information gap of a scientific model state
capabilities.description: `diagnose_information_gap(state, candidate, iteration) -> Optional[InformationGap]` joins the vendored materials layer's two axes (whether the ModelState can resolve a cell; what the evidence fails to establish against the criteria) into one gap carrying the EvidenceRequirements verbatim. science/ imports materials and never daf. Produces a diagnosis for review; changes nothing.

capabilities.label: Translate evidence requirements into neutral AcquisitionIntents
capabilities.description: `intent_for(requirement)` / `intents_for(gap)` reduce a materials EvidenceRequirement to `boundary.acquisition_intent.AcquisitionIntent{subject_natural_key, subject_kind, property, role OBSERVED|PREDICTED, target_context}`, content-hashed with evidence.identity.content_hash. Thresholds, gap category, pool state and any source/adapter/plan naming are deliberately absent. This is the mandatory, exclusive return edge from derived_state to acquisition in the control graph.

capabilities.label: Resolve which registered sources could satisfy an intent
capabilities.description: `resolve_sources(intent, capabilities, sources, vocabulary) -> CandidateSource[]` matches an AcquisitionIntent against declared `SourceCapability{properties, subject_kinds, roles, context_keys}` after one-hop alias normalisation from an explicit `Vocabulary` (EXACT_EQUIVALENT only; RELATED never matches; chains refused). Unknown is not compatible; results carry reasons and no ranking, in source_id order.

capabilities.label: Operationalise an intent into an AcquisitionPlan for a caller-chosen source
capabilities.description: `operationalize_intent(intent, source, plan_id=, parameters=, context_parameters=, mode=) -> AcquisitionPlan` verifies every key of the intent's target_context maps onto a declared source parameter and raises IntentNotOperationalizable otherwise, so scientific conditioning (datum, temperature) is never silently dropped. Pure, side-effect free; source selection stays a caller decision and execution stays `execute_plan`.

capabilities.label: Property admissibility validators (typed quantity, context, method)
capabilities.description: `quantity_is_typed` (unit, uncertainty, uncertainty_kind in stated|estimated|propagated|absent, numeric value; vectors refused UNTYPED_QUANTITY) and `no_context_free_property` (method + non-empty conditions required) return an Admissibility with named refusal codes. Applied to already-admitted evidence for canonical assertion, never as an ingest gate (ingest lives in the vendored run_scout).

capabilities.label: Aligned observation table admissibility (least_squares obligation)
capabilities.description: `observation_is_table_alignable(content)` and `is_explicitly_absent(content)` state what an Observation must carry to be joined into a (sample, variable) table: typed sample identity, typed variable identity, recoverable conditions, and an explicit absent-value representation rather than a sentinel or a dropped row. Built as DAQ's half of the 2026-08-26 joint workload decision with SCL; no table artifact is introduced.

capabilities.label: Structured measurement uncertainty and bounded evidence-lineage depth
capabilities.description: `uncertainty_corresponds_to_value` admits a measurement covariance R only when its outer dimension and per-component units correspond to an n-component value (scalar sigma on a vector, or a matrix on a scalar, refused). `lineage_depth` / `recursive_computation_is_depth_bounded` record and bound (MAX_LINEAGE_DEPTH=3) evidence-lineage depth for recursive computations with a composition guard. Both are DAQ's responses to SCL's kalman_filter_linear requirements; the five covariance shape rules stay SCL's.

capabilities.label: Assess real acquired evidence and quarantine the inadmissible
capabilities.description: `assess_pool(pool, execution_id, quarantine_store)` filters every admitted Observation whose content declares a `property`, applies `no_context_free_property` unchanged, and writes a QuarantineRecord (stage canonical_assertion) for each inadmissible candidate, returning a PropertyAdmissibilityReport whose buckets conserve. A filter, never a transformation: nothing adds or renames keys to pass the gate.

capabilities.label: Read the invariant register and verify the control graph
capabilities.description: `epistemics.invariants.load_invariants/by_status` read the 52 invariants in architecture/invariants.yaml with a closed status vocabulary (enforced, vacuously_enforced, partially_enforced, represented_unenforced, blocked, absent); `epistemics.control_graph` checks architecture/control_graph.yaml is a single 8-stage cycle whose only producer of evidence is acquisition and whose only exit from derived_state is acquisition, raising ControlGraphViolation otherwise. `core_version()` reads core.yaml (core@1.0.0 at submodule commit 5e146d5).

capabilities.label: Regenerate doctrine and agent contracts from architecture YAML
capabilities.description: `python -c "import epistemics.doctrine as d; d.write()"` projects architecture/*.yaml into docs/generated/DOCTRINE.md (word budget fails closed, vendor names linted out); `python3 architecture/build_agent_contracts.py` renders docs/generated/AGENT_*.md from daq_agent_instruments.yaml with a digest over instrument record plus schema. CI diffs both regenerations against the tree; a drift fails the conformance gate.

capabilities.label: Read the DAQ/SCL/STE exchange artifacts and their digests
capabilities.description: Content-addressed canonical YAML under architecture/exchange/: daq_capabilities.yaml (measured modality inventory, EXISTING|REUSABLE|SMALL EXTENSION|MISSING|OUT OF SCOPE, contains no workload selection), daq_requirement_response.yaml (DAQ evidence per SCL requirement row, states no status), invariant_register.yaml (three-party register), ste_invariants.yaml (reconstructed, labelled inference), plus read-only mirrors scl_requirements.yaml and scl_contract_clauses.yaml. Each has a .sha256 sidecar; the shared canonicalization fixture hashes identically in both repositories.

capabilities.label: Regenerate DAQ's exchange artifacts under the pinned canonical emitter
capabilities.description: `build_daq_capabilities.py`, `build_daq_requirement_response.py`, `build_invariant_register.py` and `build_ste_invariants.py` re-emit their artifacts through the stdlib-only `canonical_yaml.py` (sorted keys, always-quoted strings, sequence-in-sequence refused) and rewrite the .sha256 sidecars. Changing bytes of a bound artifact obliges a REISSUE of the joint decision record, which pins their digests.

capabilities.label: Verify a coordinated DAQ/SCL reissue landed in both repositories
capabilities.description: `python3 architecture/exchange/verify_pair_landed.py <repo-a> <repo-b>` asks both REMOTES (not local clones) whether each branch is in sync and compares every file both repositories hold under architecture/ byte-for-byte; exit 0 only when both are pushed and identical. Built after one half of a reissue reached its remote and the other did not.

capabilities.label: Conformance gate (CI): doctrine diff, vendored substrate unmodified, tests, types
capabilities.description: GitHub Actions workflow on every push/PR: regenerates doctrine and diffs docs/generated/, asserts `git -C vendor/scout-retrieval-agent diff` is empty, runs pytest (about 1900 tests, full history checkout so pre-registration probes can prove their expectations predate the run) and mypy over daf/ science/ boundary/ bridge/ epistemics/ session/ commerce/ tools/. Local green is a hypothesis until the pushed tree agrees.

capabilities.label: Print blank load event form and sheet header
capabilities.description: `python3 -m commerce form` prints a blank JSON events form (authority + events with kind, value, unit, basis, known_at, source) and `python3 -m commerce sheet` prints the blank CSV sheet header an operator types loads into. Pure output; the entry point for Phase 0 (one real transaction recorded by hand).

capabilities.label: Grade one load or a sheet: commitments vs outcomes
capabilities.description: `record <events.json>` and `read <sheet.csv> <authority.json>` pair every promise (rate_quoted, pickup_promised, transit_estimated) with its settlement (rate_invoiced, pickup_actual, transit_realized) through the three-store split (CommitmentStore/OutcomeStore/diverge) and print residuals. Refuses a missing authority, a known_at equal to typing time, or unlike bases. Exit 2 unusable input, 1 refusals present, 0 gradeable. Nothing is written.

capabilities.label: Append a sheet to the append-only ledger and load register
capabilities.description: `python3 -m commerce commit <sheet.csv> <authority.json>` is the ONLY commerce command that writes: it appends readable rows as events to the JSONL ledger (COMMERCE_LEDGER, default commerce-ledger.jsonl), appends load descriptions (carrier, origin, destination, month) to the register beside it, then grades the whole book. Mistakes are superseded by later entries, never edited. Refused rows are reported and not appended.

capabilities.label: Replay the ledger and show status
capabilities.description: `python3 -m commerce book` replays the JSONL ledger (current vs superseded entries, unreadable lines counted) and `status` gives one screen: ledger path, line counts, loads with unsettled promises and what each awaits. Exit 1 when the book is empty or does not conserve.

capabilities.label: Lane memory: residuals by carrier, lane, season and receiver
capabilities.description: `python3 -m commerce residuals [asof]` computes promised-vs-realized residuals per carrier, per lane, per lane-and-season and receiver appointment slippage from the book joined to the register, optionally filtered to what was knowable at `asof` (known_at, not line order). Refuses an ungrouped mean when no register exists, and states the admissibility standing of the data (a representative fixture is never admissible).

capabilities.label: Morning view: priced, blocked-with-a-named-gap, refused
capabilities.description: `python3 -m commerce morning <opportunities.json>` runs every opportunity through the gate in cost order (eligibility by activity class, compliance by credential with a cannot-determine state, then economics) and prints three lists. The middle list is the product: an unpriceable opportunity is un-ranked with WHO KNOWS the missing field, never dropped. Exit 1 if the lists do not conserve.

capabilities.label: Outbound queue: what is waiting for a person
capabilities.description: `python3 -m commerce outbound <drafts.json>` renders the OutboundQueue of agent-drafted messages (quotes, check-ins, tenders) and why each needs a human hand before it leaves the firm. Read-only rendering; nothing is sent.

capabilities.label: Carrier vetting verdict as of a date (cleared / blocked / undetermined)
capabilities.description: `python3 -m commerce vet <carrier> <asof> [booking pickup delivery]` replays persisted VettingObservations (insurance certificate window, operating authority, recent reincarnation) into a three-state Verdict as it stood at `asof`; with movement dates the insurance predicate covers the WHOLE period (SOR/2005-180 s.7 basis, CAD 100,000). Exit 0 cleared, 1 blocked, 3 undetermined, so a shell cannot collapse the third state.

capabilities.label: Exceptions queue: loads where two claims about one movement disagree
capabilities.description: `python3 -m commerce exceptions` partitions the register into consistent / divergent (tendered carrier differs from bill-of-lading carrier, the double-brokering signal) / unknowable (no BOL captured), asserts they conserve, and exits 0, 1 (divergences to work), 2 (does not conserve) or 3 (cannot be fully answered).

capabilities.label: Facility register duplicate scan (surfaced, never merged)
capabilities.description: `python3 -m commerce facilities <file.json>` normalises raw addresses (conservative fallback, or libpostal statistical parser when installed, recorded as part of the basis), scans for suspect duplicate pairs above a similarity floor, lists pairs that differ only by house number as distinct, and reports register health. Exit 1 suspects found, 3 cannot answer to zero, 0 only under the statistical normaliser with no pair above the floor.

capabilities.label: Parse CanadaBuys open-tender and award CSV feeds
capabilities.description: `commerce.canadabuys.parse_feed(bytes, source_url=, retrieved_at=)` and `commerce.award.parse_awards(...)` turn the Government of Canada open-tender (67 fields, licence ca-ogl-lgo) and award feeds into Notice/Award records with a degradation ladder carried on the result (LIVE / PUBLISHED_NO_ROWS / UNPARSEABLE / UNREACHABLE) and row accounting (admitted / rejected with reason / filtered with predicate named). The 13 contactInfo person columns have no field to land in. Bytes are caller-supplied; no fetch code exists here.

capabilities.label: Extract a structured Opportunity from a tender notice, or say why not
capabilities.description: `commerce.tender.extract(notice) -> Opportunity` grades a notice against the founding order's ten fields; five (quantity, incoterms, origin, equipment, contract value) have NO COLUMN in the CanadaBuys source and are reported as NO_COLUMN_IN_THIS_SOURCE versus EMPTY_IN_THIS_NOTICE with an attachment remedy. `census()` totals the absences across notices. `commerce.agents.tender_scout.rank/propose` orders opportunities by answerability and can only emit a Proposal to the ReviewQueue.

capabilities.label: Landed cost with stated bases, currency dates and ranges
capabilities.description: `commerce.landed_cost.assemble(components, priced_at=)` composes known / bounded / unknown Components, each carrying basis, currency, the date the currency was priced at and a completeness, into a LandedCost that yields a range or a refusal (CostRefusal) rather than a zero for an unknown component; undeclared components are printed as such. Motivated by 196/3056 awards with amount 0.00 and blank currency.

capabilities.label: Truck-legal route estimate carrying distance AND duration
capabilities.description: `commerce.mileage.truck_legal(origin, destination, distance_km=, duration_s=, ...)` / `consumer(...)` build RouteEstimates from an external router's answer, `compare()` and `validation_lane_is_discriminating()` decide whether a lane can validate a truck profile (measured 2026-08-31 on a public Valhalla instance: crossing the 4.6 m height threshold moved distance -0.3% and time +68%), and `mileage_for_pricing` refuses an estimate without duration. No routing engine is hosted here.

capabilities.label: Dispose a proposal into a commitment and issue a carrier tender
capabilities.description: `commerce.authority.dispose(proposal, verdict, disposal) -> Commitment` is the single function that turns an agent Proposal into a Commitment (issuer, authority, idempotency key, revocation path), and `commerce.tendering.issue_tender(vetting_verdict, proposal, ...)` is the only constructor of a CarrierTender, gated on a CLEARED vetting Verdict supplied by the caller. A source scan over commerce/agents/ asserts no agent can reach either. Binds the firm to a counterparty.

capabilities.label: Send an outbound message (the only way anything leaves the firm)
capabilities.description: `commerce.outbound.send(draft, sender, at=) -> Sent` is the wire boundary: agents may draft, rank, check in and propose, but only a human Actor may send, and OutboundRefusal is raised otherwise. Today `send` records the act; no mail/API transport is wired. Quotes, tenders, bookings and filings to a counterparty are escalation items under STANDING_PLAN section 4.

capabilities.label: Lint a reconnaissance record for constraints measured but not carried
capabilities.description: `commerce.recon_lint.lint(name, record) -> LintReport` reads a record's machine-readable constraints_measured block and scans every other text field for proposing sentences naming a forbidden act (defect class 8, named after a probe quoted Quebec's terms of use and then recommended a snapshot store). Surfaces candidates for a reader; deliberately does not decide.

capabilities.label: Sea Dog research session instrument: plan a work order, close a graded session
capabilities.description: `python3 -m session plan <queue.json>` ranks a researcher's question queue by expected yield per minute into a WorkOrder with per-item time boxes, dropping items that change no decision (NO_DECISION_IT_COULD_CHANGE); `close <queue.json> <capture.json>` grades the session: every ranked item lands in exactly one of worked / abandoned_at_its_box / not_reached, findings must cite sources, residue must be stated, and an acceptance test written after the work is refused. JSON in, text out; nothing persisted.

capabilities.label: Generate the representative freight fixture at scale
capabilities.description: `python3 tools/make_fixture.py --out <dir>` writes book.jsonl, register.jsonl and vetting.jsonl (40 carriers, 60 facilities, 120 lanes, 400 loads over 18 months, seed 20260831) with planted signals (over-billing carrier, lapsing insurance, slipping receiver, seasonal lane, double-brokered load, duplicate facility) in exactly the format `python3 -m commerce` reads. Every event is tagged representative_fixture and is inadmissible by construction.

nodes.name: GeoAgent Multimodal Geospatial Agent
nodes.description: Mirror of opengeos/GeoAgent (v1.8.0): a Strands-Agents-based geospatial agent layer that binds LLMs (OpenAI, Codex OAuth, Anthropic, Gemini, Bedrock, LiteLLM, Ollama) to live maps (leafmap, anymap, browser MapLibre), QGIS sessions and Earth-observation catalogs (STAC, NASA Earthdata/OPERA, GEE data catalogs, Vantor, HyperCoast, WhiteboxTools, geoai). It ships a Python API, a CLI, a Solara UI, a FastAPI WebSocket backend for browser maps, a Node/TypeScript example backend and the OpenGeoAgent QGIS plugin, with confirmation hooks before destructive or expensive tool calls. In the Notations Universe it is the geospatial perception-and-planning engine that can drive map views and catalog searches; it is an upstream mirror and must never hold canonical world state.

capabilities.label: GeoAgent.chat / stream_chat / chat_in_background
capabilities.description: Python API: run one user turn (text, or multimodal content blocks with images) through the bound Strands agent and return a GeoAgentResponse (answer_text, tool_calls, images); stream_chat yields events; chat_in_background runs on a worker thread. QGIS calls are marshalled to the GUI thread.

capabilities.label: GeoAgentConfig and provider resolution
capabilities.description: Python API: GeoAgentConfig(provider, model, temperature, max_tokens, client settings); resolve_model/get_llm/get_default_model pick a provider from environment variables (OPENAI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, GEMINI_API_KEY, LITELLM_*, OLLAMA_HOST) or explicit arguments.

capabilities.label: @geo_tool decorator and GeoToolRegistry
capabilities.description: Python API for downstream packages: @geo_tool turns a function into a Strands tool with category, safety flags (needs_confirmation) and fast-mode metadata; GeoToolRegistry lists and filters tools.

capabilities.label: Confirmation hooks
capabilities.description: Python API: ConfirmCallback/ConfirmRequest, auto_approve_all, auto_approve_safe_only and build_interrupt_on pause the agent before deleting layers, saving files or running expensive jobs; the default policy denies confirmation-required tools.

capabilities.label: create_agent with custom tools

nodes.name: Geometry-Grounded Gaussian Splatting
nodes.description: Upstream mirror of HKUST-SAIL's Geometry-Grounded Gaussian Splatting (Zhang, Jiang, Li, Shen, Tan): a 3DGS variant with multi-view geometric and NCC consistency losses, GOF densification, Mip-Splatting filters and optional spherical-Gaussian appearance, built on RaDe-GS. Given a COLMAP-registered image set it optimises a Gaussian scene, renders novel views and extracts watertight meshes (recon_post.ply) that score on DTU and Tanks-and-Temples. In the universe it is the scene-reconstruction engine whose meshes become scan evidence for the BIM state transformer. All entrypoints are GPU CLIs; it holds no canonical state of its own and must not be treated as a measured survey.

capabilities.label: Train a Gaussian scene (train.py)
capabilities.description: `python train.py -s <colmap_or_blender_dir> -m <output_dir> [-r 2] [--eval] [--use_decoupled_appearance 0|1|2|3] [--sh_degree N --sg_degree N] [--iterations 30000] [--test_iterations ...] [--save_iterations ...] [--checkpoint_iterations ...] [--start_checkpoint]`. Optimises Gaussians with photometric, depth-normal, multi-view geometry and NCC losses; writes point_cloud/iteration_N/point_cloud.ply, cameras.json, cfg_args and checkpoints under -m.

capabilities.label: Render train/test views (render.py)
capabilities.description: `python render.py -m <output_dir> [--iteration N] [--skip_train] [--skip_test]` renders every camera of the train and test splits from the trained model into <output_dir>/{train,test}/ours_N/{renders,gt}/ for metric computation.

capabilities.label: Extract mesh by TSDF fusion (mesh_extract.py)
capabilities.description: `python mesh_extract.py -m <output_dir> [--iteration N] [--num_cluster 1]` renders depth from the trained Gaussians and fuses it into a mesh; used for the DTU pipeline. Output mesh written alongside the model (recon.ply / recon_post.ply after cleaning).

capabilities.label: Extract mesh by marching tetrahedra (mesh_extract_tetrahedra.py)
capabilities.description: `python mesh_extract_tetrahedra.py -m <output_dir> [--iteration N] [--num_cluster] [--move_cpu] [--export_color]` builds a tetrahedral grid from Gaussian centres (CGAL tetra_triangulation), evaluates opacity fields and marches to a mesh; --export_color bakes vertex colors. Recommended for Tanks-and-Temples scale scenes; produces <output_dir>/recon_post.ply.

capabilities.label: Compute PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS (metric.py)
capabilities.description: `python metric.py -m <output_dir> [...]` compares renders against ground truth for each model path and writes results.json / per_view.json with PSNR, SSIM and LPIPS. (README refers to it as metrics.py; the file is metric.py.)

capabilities.label: Evaluate mesh against DTU ground truth
capabilities.description: `python evaluate_dtu_mesh.py -m <output_dir> [--scan_id N] [--DTU dtu_eval/Offical_DTU_Dataset] [--iteration 30000]` culls the extracted mesh with the DTU masks and computes Chamfer accuracy/completeness against the official DTU point clouds (DTUeval-python).

capabilities.label: Evaluate mesh on Tanks and Temples
capabilities.description: `python eval_tnt/run.py --dataset-dir <GT_TNT> --traj-path <COLMAP_SfM.log> --ply-path <output_dir>/recon_post.ply --out-dir <output_dir>/mesh` aligns the reconstruction to the GT trajectory and reports precision/recall/F-score using the official TnT toolbox.

capabilities.label: Convert output PLY to standard 3DGS PLY (ply2gs.py)
capabilities.description: `python ply2gs.py --in_ply <point_cloud.ply> --out_ply <out.ply> [--out_sh_degree 3|-1]` drops spherical-Gaussian attributes and bakes the 3D filter into scale/opacity so the scene loads in SuperSplat, LichtFeld Studio and other standard Gaussian viewers.

capabilities.label: Batch train/extract/evaluate scripts
capabilities.description: scripts/dtu.sh, scripts/tnt.sh, scripts/mip360.sh loop train.py -> mesh extraction -> evaluation over each benchmark scene with the paper's settings (-r 2 --use_decoupled_appearance 3). Dataset paths are hard-coded and must be edited.

capabilities.label: SIBR network viewer socket during training
capabilities.description: train.py listens on --ip 127.0.0.1 --port 6009 for the SIBR remote viewer (SIBR_viewers/, patched for embree4/newer Boost) which streams interactive renders of the scene while it optimises. Wire protocol is the original graphdeco 3DGS network_gui.

capabilities.label: COLMAP scene input contract
capabilities.description: `-s` directory with images/ (or --images name) and sparse/0/{cameras.bin, images.bin, points3D.bin} (or .txt). Optional resolution downscale via -r; --eval holds out every 8th view (llffhold=8). DTU expects the 2DGS-preprocessed layout; TnT the PGSR preprocessing.

capabilities.label: NeRF-synthetic (Blender) input contract
capabilities.description: `-s` directory with transforms_train.json / transforms_test.json and PNG frames, selected automatically when no sparse/ folder exists; --white_background controls compositing.

capabilities.label: Trained model directory contract
capabilities.description: <output_dir>/point_cloud/iteration_N/point_cloud.ply (Gaussian attributes incl. filter_3D and optional SG terms), cameras.json, cfg_args, chkpntN.pth, and after extraction recon.ply / recon_post.ply meshes. recon_post.ply is the artefact other ecosystem nodes consume.

nodes.name: God's Eye View
nodes.description: Fork of bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view: a browser spy-satellite simulator that turns public signals into a place. A vanilla-JS CesiumJS globe on Google Photorealistic 3D Tiles renders thirteen live layers (OpenSky/adsb.lol flights, AISStream vessels, CelesTrak satellites via SGP4, USGS earthquakes, TomTom/OSM traffic, ~800 projected public cameras, Radio Browser stations, GBFS bikeshare, NASA FIRMS fires, Launch Library 2 missions, OSM military installations) plus bundled datacenters, dams and submarine cables, with cockpit view, sensor-look shaders, detection overlay, scene director and an OpenAI Realtime voice agent. The server is a set of Vite dev/preview middlewares under /api/* that broker keys, cache and budget upstream calls; there is no database and nothing is stored beyond caches. nodes.name: Information Systems Archive
nodes.description: Off-repository archive mirror (shipping order S-2) of Sea Dog Terminal's data archive, the lineage now served by Payload Terminal V0. What matters here is the UNRECONSTRUCTABLE class: UN Comtrade captures. Comtrade keeps one version per dataset and revises in place, so a lost capture is a knowledge state that cannot be recovered from anywhere, including UNSD. The mirror holds the 2026-08-27 Comtrade retrievals for copper ore (HS 2603) and refined copper (HS 7403) reporters Chile, Peru, China, DRC and Indonesia, the comtrade-* served snapshots and data-availability vintages, plus refetchable-at-risk Open Ownership captures and refetchable USGS MCS, CFTC, Yahoo, Westmetall and EDGAR snapshots, every file indexed in MANIFEST.json with a sha256 and durability class and checked by verify.mjs. It is a second GitHub repository guarding against repo-level accidents, not a provider-independent backup; it must never be treated as current data (byte identity is coverage for divergence, not currency) and never be edited by hand.

capabilities.label: Read the durability manifest
capabilities.description: sea-dog-terminal/data-archive/MANIFEST.json lists every mirrored file with path, sha256, bytes and durability class (counts: 14 unreconstructable, 8 refetchable_at_risk, 6 refetchable, 1 documentation). Generated upstream by scripts/archive-manifest.mjs; the label a pruner needs in a year.

capabilities.label: Verify the mirror against its manifest
capabilities.description: `node sea-dog-terminal/verify.mjs` hashes every manifest entry under sea-dog-terminal/ and prints `OK: N files verified` (exit 0) or `MISMATCH <path>` lines and `FAILED: n mismatches` (exit 1). Detects corruption or divergence in the mirror; does not detect staleness.

capabilities.label: Read unreconstructable UN Comtrade raw captures
capabilities.description: sea-dog-terminal/data-archive/comtrade/<retrieval-date>/<reporter>-<hs>-<flow>-<year>.json holds the verbatim Comtrade API response ({elapsedTime, count, data[...]} rows with reporterCode, partnerCode, cmdCode, flowCode, qty, netWgt, primaryValue...) for each successful live retrieval, keyed by retrieval date and request key. Eleven files for 2026-08-27 (152/604/360 x 2603 exports 2017-2024; 156 x 2603/7403 imports 2023; 180 x 7403 exports 2023); five are the 11-byte empty-result body.

capabilities.label: Read the served Comtrade snapshots and flow vintages
capabilities.description: sea-dog-terminal/src/data/economy/snapshots/comtrade-copper.json, comtrade-flow-vintages.json and comtrade-da.json (unreconstructable class) are the vintages the terminal serves from; comtrade-da.json records per reporter/period firstReleased and lastReleased so `as_known_then` blindness before the held version's release date is labelled rather than silent.

capabilities.label: Read refetchable-at-risk Open Ownership captures
capabilities.description: sea-dog-terminal/data-archive/openownership/2026-08-27/: S3 export listings (s3-list.xml, s3-public-exports.xml), BODS statement samples (control-glencore-sample.jsonl, match-antamina.jsonl), register search pages (search-antamina.html, search-collahuasi.html) and scan-summary.txt (statements=32813462 antamina=1 collahuasi=0 glencore_control=53) from a frozen 2023 export of a retired product.

capabilities.label: Read refetchable economy snapshots
capabilities.description: sea-dog-terminal/src/data/economy/snapshots/: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries 2024/2025 world copper and 2025 aluminium (.ts), cftc-copper-1yr.json, yahoo-hg-10y.json, sec-edgar-recon.json (refetchable) and westmetall-lme-stocks.json (refetchable_at_risk, single republisher). Loss costs a re-fetch, not a vintage.

capabilities.label: Restore the archive into a terminal checkout
capabilities.description: Documented restore path: clone this repo, run verify.mjs, copy sea-dog-terminal/data-archive/ and sea-dog-terminal/src/data/economy/snapshots/ over the same paths in a checkout of the main repository, then run `npx vitest run src/lib/economy/archiveManifest.test.ts` there (green = byte-identical). Executed once at mirror creation (ledger phase 36). Overwrites files in another repository.

capabilities.label: Refresh the mirror after an archival
capabilities.description: Update cadence: mirror after every archival (any new day-directory under data-archive/comtrade/). The main repository's CI verifies its own manifest; this mirror is refreshed manually or by operator automation. No script exists here; the refresh is a copy plus commit.

nodes.name: LichtFeld Studio
nodes.description: Upstream mirror of MrNeRF's LichtFeld Studio: a native C++23/CUDA workstation for 3D Gaussian Splatting that trains scenes from COLMAP datasets, inspects them in real time, edits Gaussian selections and scene nodes with undo/redo, and exports to PLY, SOG, SPZ, USD, RAD or a standalone HTML viewer. It is where a human operates on splat scenes; agents reach the same surface through a local MCP HTTP server (http://127.0.0.1:45677/mcp) with discovery resources and mutation tools, an embedded Python API (`import lichtfeld as lf`) and a manifest-driven Python plugin system. It must never be the canonical store of scene state: it consumes datasets and checkpoints from disk and hands exports back to the ecosystem. NVIDIA GPU required; Windows binaries via the LichtFeld portal, Linux via source or the docker/ image.

capabilities.label: Train from a COLMAP dataset (CLI / headless)
capabilities.description: `LichtFeld-Studio -d <data-path> -o <output-path> [--headless] [-i iter] [--strategy mcmc|default] [--sh-degree N] [--max-cap N] [--config file] [--init ply] [--import-cameras] [--images dir] [--test-every N] [--timelapse-every N] [--ppisp-sidecar] [--python-script file]`. Headless mode requires --data-path or --resume. Writes checkpoints and PLY snapshots to the output path.

capabilities.label: Open a PLY/checkpoint in the viewer (-v)
capabilities.description: `LichtFeld-Studio -v <file.ply>` or `--resume <checkpoint>` launches the GUI on an existing scene without training; the app also starts with no arguments as an empty workstation.

capabilities.label: Convert/export a scene from the CLI (-f)
capabilities.description: Export sub-parser: `-f/--format ply|sog|spz|html|usd|usda|usdc|rad [--sog-iterations K] [--sh-degree N]` converts a loaded PLY/checkpoint into the chosen delivery format without the GUI.

capabilities.label: Plugin scaffolding and validation CLI
capabilities.description: `LichtFeld-Studio plugin create <name>` (package + .venv + VS Code config under ~/.lichtfeld/plugins/), `plugin check <name>` (validate manifest/structure), `plugin list` (installed plugins).

capabilities.label: Local MCP HTTP endpoint
capabilities.description: The GUI application starts an MCP server with resources enabled on http://127.0.0.1:45677/mcp (Streamable HTTP). `scripts/lichtfeld_mcp_bridge.py` (wired by .mcp.json) launches the app and proxies stdio MCP to it; LICHTFELD_MCP_ENDPOINT overrides the URL. Initialize, then tools/list and resources/list.

capabilities.label: MCP discovery resources (runtime/ui/scene/selection/history)

nodes.name: LingBot-Depth (Masked Depth Modeling)
nodes.description: Upstream mirror of Robbyant's LingBot-Depth: a ViT-L/14 masked-depth-modeling model that refines incomplete, noisy RGB-D sensor depth into metric-accurate depth maps and 3D point clouds. In the Notations Universe it is a perception primitive: given an RGB image, a raw depth map and camera intrinsics it proposes clean geometry for scan-to-BIM registration, scene reconstruction and downstream 3D engines. It is a library plus example CLI with no server; every run is a GPU compute job that downloads weights from Hugging Face. It must never be treated as canonical geometry: its outputs are model predictions to be registered as evidence, not as measured state.

Reads examples/<N>/{rgb.png|jpg, raw_depth.png (16-bit mm), intrinsics.txt}, loads the checkpoint (Hugging Face download on first run), runs MDMModel.infer and writes result/{depth_input.npy, depth_refined.npy (float32 m), depth_input.png, depth_refined.png, depth_comparison.png, rgb.png, point_cloud.ply}.

capabilities.label: Load MDMModel checkpoint (Python API)
capabilities.description: `mdm.model.v2.MDMModel.from_pretrained(name_or_path, model_kwargs=None, **hf_kwargs)`: loads a local model.pt or downloads `model.pt` from a Hugging Face model repo (robbyant/lingbot-depth-pretrain-vitl-14-v0.5 recommended; -v0.1; postrain-dc-vitl14 for sparse completion). Returns a torch.nn.Module to move to device.

capabilities.label: Refine depth and lift to point cloud (MDMModel.infer)

Depth input is required in this version.

capabilities.description: Same inputs as infer; returns the encoder's joint RGB-depth feature tokens instead of decoded depth, for downstream representation learning (tracking, manipulation policies).

nodes.name: Matrix-3D
nodes.description: Upstream mirror of Skywork's Matrix-3D v0.1: omnidirectional explorable 3D world generation. A three-stage GPU pipeline turns a text prompt or a single image into a panorama (FLUX.1 LoRA), the panorama plus a camera trajectory into a panoramic tour video (Wan2.1 / Wan2.2-5B LoRA conditioned on MoGe-depth warped renders), and the video into a 3D Gaussian scene (optimisation-based Pano_GS_Opt or feed-forward PanoLRM). In the universe it is a generative world model: it fabricates plausible scenes, so its outputs are synthetic and must never be registered as observed geometry. Exposed as CLI stages, generate.sh and a Gradio demo; checkpoints are pulled from Hugging Face.

capabilities.label: One-command world generation (generate.sh)
capabilities.description: Runs Step1 text-to-panorama, Step2 torchrun panorama-to-video at 720p, Step3 optimisation-based 3D scene extraction into output/example1. Edit the prompt/output_dir inside the script; ~1 hour for 720p on an A800.

capabilities.label: Download model checkpoints
capabilities.description: `python code/download_checkpoints.py` pulls Ruicheng/moge-vitl, Iceclear/StableSR and Skywork/Matrix-3D artefacts (text2panoimage_lora.safetensors, pano_video_gen_480p.ckpt, pano_video_gen_720p.bin, pano_video_gen_720p_5b.safetensors, pano_lrm_480p.pt) into ./checkpoints/{moge,StableSR,flux_lora,pano_lrm,Wan-AI/wan_lora}.

capabilities.label: Step 1: text/image to panorama (panoramic_image_generation.py)
capabilities.description: `python code/panoramic_image_generation.py --mode t2p --prompt "..." --output_path DIR` or `--mode i2p --input_image_path img.jpg [--fov F]` plus --seed/--device. Writes DIR/pano_img.jpg (equirectangular) and DIR/prompt.txt. Externally produced panoramas can be dropped into the same layout to skip this stage.

capabilities.label: Step 2: panorama to panoramic tour video (torchrun)
capabilities.description: `torchrun --nproc_per_node N code/panoramic_image_to_video.py --inout_dir DIR --resolution 480|720 [--movement_mode straight|s_curve|l_curve|r_curve] [--angle deg] [--movement_range 0-0.8] [--json_path cams.json] [--seed] [--use_5b_model] [--enable_vram_management]`. Estimates depth with MoGe, warps the panorama along the trajectory into rendered_rgb.mp4 / rendered_mask.mp4 conditions, and generates DIR/pano_video.mp4 (960x480 or 1440x720, 81 frames) with the Wan video LoRA. Multi-GPU via xfuser.

capabilities.label: Step 3a: optimisation-based 3D scene extraction
capabilities.description: `python code/panoramic_video_to_3DScene.py --inout_dir DIR --resolution 480|720 [--device]`. Optionally super-resolves the video (VideoSR/StableSR), initialises Gaussians from panoramic frames and runs Pano_GS_Opt training (3000 iterations); copies point_cloud/iteration_3000/point_cloud.ply to DIR/generated_3dgs_opt.ply.

capabilities.label: Step 3b: feed-forward PanoLRM reconstruction (480p)

capabilities.description: `python code/generate_example_camera.py` writes test_cam_{front,back,left,right}.json: 81 4x4 world-to-camera matrices (OpenCV convention) as a JSON list, the format accepted by --json_path / --pose_path. Adapt the script for custom rails.
