nodes.name: Notations Corpus Graph
nodes.description: A provenance-tracked corpus graph linking bespoke-polymer structure and formulation to the instrument measurements made on them and to the properties derived from those measurements. Four layers (chemistry: Substance/Monomer/Polymer/Formulation; process: ProcessStep -> Sample -> Specimen; measurement: Instrument + Method -> Measurement -> Signal; inference: PropertyValue always pointing at its Signal) with content-addressed node identity so re-ingest is idempotent, and every derived number keeps its trace and method. Parsers for JCAMP-DX, Bruker TopSpin, SEC/GPC ASCII, DSC/TGA ASCII and mzML decode into a neutral intermediate representation; derivations recover Mn/Mw/dispersity, Tg/Tm/Tc, Td5/Td50, MALDI repeat units and band assignments, and property terms declare dimension and plausible range so bad units fail at the ingest boundary. Runtime is stdlib-only so it runs on instrument workstations. It is the scientific information library of the universe: a `ncg` CLI and Python API over a JSONL(.gz) corpus file, no HTTP or MCP server, and it must never silently merge two materials or let an instrument's self-reported answer replace the traced one.

capabilities.label: Ingest instrument exports into a corpus
capabilities.description: `ncg ingest <paths...> [-o corpus.jsonl(.gz)] [--into existing] [--samples manifest.json] [--parser name] [--no-derive] [--no-recursive] [--json] [--strict]` walks files and directories (Bruker experiment directories as units), sniffs a parser per file, de-duplicates by content sha256, maps to the schema, resolves sample keys, derives properties, validates invariants and writes the corpus atomically. --strict exits non-zero on any failed path or validation problem.

capabilities.label: Validate a corpus against schema invariants
capabilities.description: `ncg validate corpus.jsonl.gz [--json]` loads the corpus and runs CorpusGraph.validate: relation source/target kind rules, property dimension and range checks, dangling references. Exit 0 ok, 1 with problems listed.

capabilities.label: Describe a corpus
capabilities.description: `ncg summary corpus [--json]` prints node and edge counts, nodes by kind, edges by relation and measurements by technique.

capabilities.label: Show one sample and everything measured on it
capabilities.description: `ncg show corpus <lab_id> [--json]` lists, for the sample(s) whose folded lab id matches, every measurement (technique, started_at, signals) and every property (term, value, technique, derivation method, confidence). Exit 1 with the known-sample list when nothing matches.

capabilities.label: Report which parser claims each path
capabilities.description: `ncg detect <paths...>` discovers candidate inputs and prints each parser's sniff confidence per path without ingesting anything.

capabilities.label: List registered parsers
capabilities.description: `ncg formats [--json]` lists parser name, format, version and extensions: jcamp-dx (.jdx .dx .jcm .jcamp), bruker-topspin (directory), sec-ascii, thermal-ascii (.csv .txt .tsv .asc .dat), mzml (.mzml .mzml.gz). CI checks this command runs from an install.

capabilities.label: List the property vocabulary
capabilities.description: `ncg terms [--json]` lists every PropertyTerm with its physical dimension, label, applicable techniques and plausible [minimum, maximum] range (e.g. Mn, Mw, dispersity, Tg onset/midpoint/end, delta Cp, Tm, Tc, Td5, Td50, repeat unit mass, signal-to-noise).

capabilities.label: Python API: ingest() and discover()
capabilities.description: `ncg.ingest.pipeline.ingest(roots, graph=, resolver=, registry=, recursive=, derive=, parser_name=)` returns an IngestReport (graph, per-file outcomes with status/parser/runs/properties/technique/message, warnings, seconds, format_text(), summary()); `discover(roots, recursive=)` yields candidate paths treating Bruker directories as units. Files already present by sha256 are skipped, so re-ingesting a growing share is idempotent.

capabilities.label: Python API: CorpusGraph query and traversal
capabilities.description: `CorpusGraph.of_kind(kind)`, `find(kind, **criteria)`, `first(...)`, `get/node(id)`, `out_edges/in_edges(id, relation)`, `neighbours`, `traverse`, `path_exists`, `sample_of(node_id)`, `measurements_of(sample_id)`, `signals_of(measurement_id)`, `properties_of(sample_id)`, `summary()`, `validate()`. Read-only over an in-memory graph.

capabilities.label: Python API: CorpusGraph add, connect, remove, merge
capabilities.description: `add(node)`, `add_all(nodes)`, `connect(source, relation, target, **attrs)`, `add_edge(edge)`, `remove(node_id)` and `merge_graph(other)` change the in-memory graph; nodes are content-addressed so adding the same fact twice converges on one node, and relation rules are enforced at edge creation.

capabilities.label: Python API: save and load the JSONL corpus
capabilities.description: `CorpusGraph.save(path)` streams a header record (format_version 1, node_count, edge_count) then node and edge records as JSON lines, gzip when the suffix is .gz, written to a .partial sibling and renamed so an interrupted save never replaces a good corpus; `CorpusGraph.load(path)` reads it back.

capabilities.label: File contract: corpus JSONL(.gz) format v1
capabilities.description: One header line {record: header, format_version, node_count, edge_count}, then {record: node, kind, id, ...} and {record: edge, relation, source, target, ...} lines in sorted id order. Node kinds: source_file, substance, monomer, polymer, formulation, process_step, sample, specimen, instrument, method, measurement, signal, property. Relations: has_component, derived_from_monomer, input_to, produced, follows, realises, aliquot_of, measured, used_instrument, used_method, yielded, derived_from, characterises, extracted_from, contradicts, corroborates.

capabilities.label: File contract: sample alias manifest
capabilities.description: `--samples samples.json` / `SampleKeyResolver.from_manifest(path)`: {aliases: {free text -> lab id}, patterns: [regex with one capture group]} maps instrument sample strings onto lab ids explicitly. Without it the resolver takes the leading token conservatively and an unfamiliar trailing phrase creates a separate sample rather than silently merging; every resolution records how it was reached.

capabilities.label: Parser: JCAMP-DX 4.24 / 5.01
capabilities.description: Decodes .jdx/.dx/.jcm/.jcamp spectra (FTIR, Raman, NMR, MS) into RawDataset/RawRun/RawSignal, checking DIF Y-checkpoints and per-line abscissas against the declared axis so dropped lines are flagged (file still ingested, flagged). Registered in ncg.ingest.REGISTRY; `Parser.sniff(path, head)` and `parse(path)` are the adapter protocol.

capabilities.label: Parser: Bruker TopSpin NMR dataset directories
capabilities.description: Reads a TopSpin experiment directory (acqus, processed 1r data) as one unit for 1H and 13C NMR; discovery never descends into it so one experiment is never ingested several times.

capabilities.label: Parser: SEC / GPC ASCII exports
capabilities.description: Reads Agilent, Waters, Malvern, PSS and Tosoh chromatogram exports (.csv .txt .tsv .asc .dat), choosing the delimiter and decimal mark by trying them so European decimal-comma exports parse; yields chromatogram signals and any vendor-reported calibration and moments for comparison.

capabilities.label: Parser: DSC / TGA ASCII exports
capabilities.description: Reads TA Instruments, Mettler STARe and Netzsch Proteus thermogram exports with time, temperature and heat-flow or mass columns; heating rate is later measured from the columns rather than read from the method string.

capabilities.label: Parser: mzML (HUPO-PSI) mass spectra
capabilities.description: Streams .mzml / .mzml.gz files for MALDI, decoding binary data arrays (numpy when available, stdlib otherwise) into mass spectra and peak tables.

capabilities.label: Derive SEC molar-mass moments
capabilities.description: `fit_calibration`, `molar_mass_at`, `moments`: fits the column calibration (detecting axes swapped by checking molar mass falls as elution volume rises), sets integration limits from detector noise, reports mass outside the calibrated range instead of extrapolating, and derives Mn, Mw, Mz, Mp and dispersity; vendor-reported values are stored alongside and compared.

capabilities.label: Derive DSC and TGA properties
capabilities.description: `glass_transition` (onset/midpoint/end and delta Cp found as a persistent baseline offset, sign-convention independent), `melting_peak` (Tm, Tc, enthalpy of fusion with the heating rate measured from the data and a >5% disagreement reported) and `tga_features` (Td5, Td50, extrapolated onset, peak mass-loss temperature, residue).

capabilities.label: Derive MALDI oligomer series properties
capabilities.description: `analyse_series` and `moments_from_peaks` recover repeat-unit mass, end-group mass modulo the repeat unit (absolute DP only when a known end group and cation are given), Mn, Mw, dispersity and DPn from a MALDI peak lattice.

capabilities.label: Derive properties for one run with provenance
capabilities.description: `derive_for_run(run, ...)` dispatches by technique to the SEC, thermal, mass-spec and vibrational (band positions with candidate assignments) derivations and signal-to-noise for every trace, emitting PropertyValue nodes whose Derivation records method and parameters and which point at the Signal they came from; values outside a term's plausible range are rejected at the boundary.

capabilities.label: Python API: quantities and unit conversion
capabilities.description: `ncg.Quantity`, `parse_quantity(text, default_unit=)`, `convert(value, from_unit, to_unit)`, `dimension_of`, `canonical_unit`, `is_known_unit`, `mean_quantity` — dimension-checked units so a Tg in g/mol fails with UnitError rather than entering the corpus.

capabilities.label: Python contract: node types, vocabularies and codec
capabilities.description: `ncg.schema.nodes` dataclasses (SourceFile, Substance, Monomer, Polymer, Formulation, ProcessStep, Sample, Specimen, Instrument, Method, Measurement, Signal, PropertyValue with Component/Peak/Derivation value objects), `ncg.schema.vocab` enums (Technique, Architecture, ProcessKind, SignalKind, PropertyTerm), `ncg.schema.edges.Relation` and `node_from_dict` / `encode_dataclass` for round-tripping. SchemaError is raised on any invariant violation.

nodes.name: OSIRIS Intelligence Layer (payload-intel)
nodes.description: A small Express 5 service (intel/server.js, port 4000, container payload-intel) that acts as the ontology brain other Payload services query through GET /resolve: it ingests the OpenSanctions OFAC SDN CSV into an in-memory alias-normalised index refreshed every 24 h, queries Wikidata SPARQL and entity search on demand behind an LRU cache, and enriches IP addresses through ip-api.com and RIPE Stat, returning every answer as a typed {nodes, links} graph with SANCTIONS MATCH edges. Outbound requests are restricted to an allowlist of five domains, SPARQL inputs are sanitized, and each client IP is limited to 30 requests per minute. It holds no canonical state and writes nothing durable; the index is rebuilt at boot and a failed refresh keeps the stale copy. It must never become a person-profiling service: the person and abuse-contact paths it still serves sit in tension with the terminal's collection policy and are flagged for review.

Returns {nodes[{id,label,type,properties}], links[{source,target,label}], entity, source, sanctions_index_size, timestamp}; cached 24 h in an LRU of 10,000 keys; Cache-Control s-maxage=3600. Rate-limited 30/min per client IP; id sanitized, 2-200 chars.

capabilities.label: Resolve a vessel by IMO or name
capabilities.description: GET /resolve?type=vessel&id=<imo|name>: Wikidata SPARQL by IMO number (P458) or English label under ship subclasses, yielding OWNED BY, OPERATED BY and FLAG STATE links, plus OFAC SDN cross-reference. Returns {nodes[{id,label,type,properties}], links[{source,target,label}], entity, source, sanctions_index_size, timestamp}; cached 24 h in an LRU of 10,000 keys; Cache-Control s-maxage=3600. Rate-limited 30/min per client IP; id sanitized, 2-200 chars.

Returns {nodes[{id,label,type,properties}], links[{source,target,label}], entity, source, sanctions_index_size, timestamp}; cached 24 h in an LRU of 10,000 keys; Cache-Control s-maxage=3600. nodes.name: Payload OCR Agent
nodes.description: Document perception subsystem for the Payload operating system: it turns freight paperwork (rate confirmations, bills of lading, proofs of delivery, invoices, scans, PDFs) into structured, provenance-preserving Observations. Its output unit is an ObservationBundle - every field carries verbatim raw text, a normalized value, an evidence location (page + character span into preserved OCR text), separate extraction-confidence / source-reliability / verification fields, a temporal frame and full execution identity - wrapped as a CanonicalStateCandidate with adjudication fixed at 'pending'. It emits only OBSERVED / EXTRACTED / INFERRED states, detects conflicts without resolving them, proposes entity candidates without resolving identity, and hands bundles to the host's EvidencePool through an EvidenceSink port. It must never become a source of truth: no canonical-state types, stores or writers exist in the package, and tests audit the source tree to keep it that way. The OCR model (Mistral today) sits behind the OCRModel seam.

capabilities.label: ocr.inspect_document - perception summary
capabilities.description: Ingests an artifact (content bytes, mimeType, fileName, receivedAt, source) and runs full-document OCR via the provider; returns InspectResult {artifactId (content-addressed), pageCount, blocksPerPage, tablesPerPage, textCharsPerPage, warnings} or a typed Refusal (UNSUPPORTED_MIME, OCR_FAILED, DOCUMENT_UNREADABLE, PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE...). Reads the document; writes nothing.

capabilities.label: ocr.classify_document - typed classification
capabilities.description: OCRs the artifact and classifies it as one of RATE_CONFIRMATION, BILL_OF_LADING, PROOF_OF_DELIVERY, INVOICE, PURCHASE_ORDER, CARRIER_PACKET, INSURANCE_CERTIFICATE, CUSTOMS_DOCUMENT, PACKING_LIST, SHIPPER_DOCUMENT, CONTRACT, EMAIL_ATTACHMENT, OTHER or UNKNOWN with a confidence; UNKNOWN is the floor (CLASSIFICATION_FLOOR 0.5). A proposal about document kind, never about truth of contents.

capabilities.label: ocr.extract_fields - full pipeline to ObservationBundle
capabilities.description: Runs the staged pipeline: ingest/identify -> raw perception -> classify -> schema-guided extraction with versioned prompt -> zod validation + consistency checks (report, never repair) -> normalization keeping raw -> Observation construction -> conflict detection -> entity candidates -> EvidenceSink registration -> CanonicalStateCandidate. Returns PipelineOutput {bundle, candidate, receipt, entityCandidates, validationIssues, classification, artifactReprocessed}. Registers candidates with the host-supplied sink (idempotent under contentHash+executionKey); never touches canonical state.

capabilities.label: ocr.extract_table - tables of an artifact
capabilities.description: Ingests the artifact and returns the provider's table perception (OCRTable[] per page) in provider-neutral shape, or a typed Refusal.

capabilities.label: ocr.find_evidence - observation id to evidence location
capabilities.description: Looks up an observationId inside a bundle and returns {observation, location} where EvidenceLocation is text_span {artifactId, page, start, end} | page_only | region (bounding box) | artifact_only. Refuses FIELD_NOT_FOUND otherwise. No model call.

capabilities.label: ocr.validate_extraction - consistency issues of a bundle
capabilities.description: Surfaces the validation issues attached at extraction time (e.g. arithmetic_mismatch: charges vs printed total, inverted pickup/delivery windows) as ValidationIssue[] {kind, field, detail} without re-running a model. Issues are reported, never repaired.

capabilities.label: ocr.compare_documents - cross-document conflict detection
capabilities.description: Given two bundles with claimant labels, joins observations on the curated shared-subject map (no fuzzy joins) and returns ConflictRecord[] {conflictId, subjectKey, relation contradiction | supersession_candidate | under_determined, observationIds, detail, remedy}. All readings retained, no winner chosen, recency never a tiebreak; resolution is explicitly downstream.

capabilities.label: ocr.create_observation - bundle to canonical-state CANDIDATE
capabilities.description: Wraps a sealed ObservationBundle as CanonicalStateCandidate {kind: 'canonical_state_candidate', adjudication: 'pending', bundle, requiredPath: ['EvidencePool','EntityResolution','Validation']}. Refuses CANONICAL_STATE_BREACH if any observation claims a non-perception status or a verification other than UNVERIFIED. The only shape allowed to travel toward canonical state; adjudication happens downstream.

capabilities.label: processDocument(deps, req) pipeline entry
capabilities.description: Public TypeScript entry for the staged lifecycle behind ocr.extract_fields. PipelineDeps = {provider: OCRModel, sink: EvidenceSink, prompts?, telemetry?, register?: ArtifactRegister, now?}. Returns Result<PipelineOutput>; PIPELINE_VERSION is stamped into every ExtractionMeta.

capabilities.label: ingestArtifact / ArtifactRegister (INGEST, IDENTIFY)
capabilities.description: Content-addressed artifact identity: IngestRequest {content: Uint8Array, mimeType, fileName?, receivedAt, source, maxBytes? (default 50 MiB)} -> ArtifactWithContent with artifactId derived from bytes; refuses unsupported MIME types and oversize input. ArtifactRegister records Sightings so the same bytes seen twice never become two evidence objects.

capabilities.label: OCRModel provider interface
capabilities.description: The only model surface the system sees: {providerName, deterministic, extractDocument(artifact), extractPages(artifact, pages), extractLayout(artifact), extractTables(artifact), extractStructured({artifact, jsonSchema, schemaVersion, prompt, promptVersion})}, all returning Result in the agent's refusal vocabulary. Implementations: MistralOCRProvider (data-URL documents, markdown pages, document_annotation JSON-schema extraction) and FixtureOCRProvider (deterministic test corpus). A structural test fails if provider names leak outside src/model/providers/.

capabilities.label: createProvider / providerFromEnv
capabilities.description: Configuration-time construction of the OCR provider: createProvider({provider:'mistral', config}) or ({provider:'fixture', fixtures}); providerFromEnv() selects Mistral when MISTRAL_API_KEY is set and otherwise refuses PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE with a remedy. Hosts must not import MistralOCRProvider outside configuration code.

capabilities.label: Freight document schemas (zod) and registry
capabilities.description: schemaFor(documentType) / registeredSchemas(): versioned zod schemas for RATE_CONFIRMATION, BILL_OF_LADING, PROOF_OF_DELIVERY and INVOICE, each paired with a versioned prompt; the JSON Schema handed to extractStructured is derived from the zod schema and its schemaVersion is stamped on every observation.

capabilities.label: Deterministic normalizers (money, weight, temporal)
capabilities.description: Normalize money ('$1,850 USD' -> 1850 + USD), weight ('42,000 lbs' -> 42000 + lb) and document-stated times ('Sept 3 8:00 AM' -> '--09-03T08:00' at written precision, zone 'unstated') while always keeping raw beside the value. Divergence between the normalizer and the provider's typed reading is retained on the observation and warned on the bundle.

capabilities.label: buildObservation / observationsFromExtraction
capabilities.description: Construction checkpoint for the Observation unit: refuses (ObservationConstructionError) unless source location, temporal frame and execution identity are present, and asserts the epistemic state is OBSERVED, EXTRACTED or INFERRED (INFERRED requires a stated rule and input observation ids). observationsFromExtraction flattens a validated extraction into observations; locateInPages finds verbatim spans in preserved page text. Typed values without a verbatim source are dropped as unwarranted.

capabilities.label: EvidenceSink port and registerBundle bridge
capabilities.description: Outbound port to the host's authoritative EvidencePool: EvidenceSink.register(bundle) -> Result<EvidenceReceipt {bundleId, evidenceIds (pool-assigned, aligned to observations), deduplicated, registeredAt}>, required idempotent under (artifact.contentHash, extraction.executionKey). registerBundle re-checks warrants before crossing; RecordingEvidenceSink is an in-memory stub for tests/demo, explicitly not an evidence store. The agent never mints evidence ids.

capabilities.label: detectConflicts(SubjectObservation[])
capabilities.description: Library entry behind ocr.compare_documents: classifies incompatible readings of a shared subject into contradiction / supersession_candidate / under_determined, keeping every supporting observation and prescribing a remedy for downstream reconciliation. Vocabulary matches the Terminal's claim relations so it can be ingested without translation.

capabilities.label: candidatesFromObservations - EntityCandidate emission
capabilities.description: Derives typed EntityCandidate {kind shipment|load|carrier|shipper|consignee|facility|address|lane|commodity|equipment|invoice|order, raw verbatim text, observationId, location, resolution: 'unresolved', schemeHint?} from a bundle. Addresses are candidates for the spatial layer (address -> facility -> coordinates -> network node -> route) to resolve; nothing is merged on similarity here.

capabilities.label: envelopeDocumentText / findInjectionAttempts
capabilities.description: Document content is data, never instructions: OCR text is wrapped in a delimiter-neutralized DOCUMENT CONTENT envelope before any prompt, and mechanical injection detection returns InjectionFinding[] surfaced as bundle warnings only (never blocking, never acted on).

capabilities.label: Versioned prompt registry
capabilities.description: PromptRegistry / defaultPromptRegistry load prompts/*.vN.md (classify_document, extract_rate_confirmation, extract_bol, extract_pod, extract_invoice); prompt identity = name + content hash and the promptVersion is recorded on every extraction. Prompts are never inline literals.

capabilities.label: TelemetrySink / ExecutionRecord
capabilities.description: Operational telemetry channel: ExecutionRecord carries counts, provider/model/prompt/schema/pipeline versions, latency and refusal codes and has structurally no slot for a document value; InMemoryTelemetry is the default sink. Telemetry and evidence never share a channel.

capabilities.label: ObservationBundle / Observation (the emitted evidence contract)
capabilities.description: Observation {observationId 'obs:<hash>' deterministic under (artifact, field, executionKey), field subject key e.g. 'rate_confirmation/total_rate', value {raw, normalized, unit} | typed Absence (NOT_PRESENT, NOT_READABLE, NOT_EXTRACTED, NOT_APPLICABLE, UNKNOWN, CONFLICTING), status OBSERVED|EXTRACTED|INFERRED, extractionConfidence, rawConfidence?, sourceReliability 'unassessed', verificationStatus 'UNVERIFIED', location, temporal, extraction, inference?, notes?}. Bundle adds bundleId, artifact, documentType, classificationConfidence, conflicts, ambiguities, warnings, refusals, ocrExecutions.

capabilities.label: CanonicalStateCandidate (adjudication: pending)
capabilities.description: The only shape that may travel toward canonical state: {kind 'canonical_state_candidate', adjudication 'pending' (no constructor argument exists to change it), bundle, requiredPath ['EvidencePool','EntityResolution','Validation']}. The boundary test walks the source tree and fails if any module outside src/canonical/ names canonical state.

capabilities.label: ExtractionMeta / execution identity
capabilities.description: Every bundle and observation carries {modelProvider, model, modelVersion, promptVersion, schemaVersion, pipelineVersion, executionKey = hash(contentHash, provider, modelVersion, promptVersion, schemaVersion, pipelineVersion), executionId per run}. Same artifact + same configuration -> same observationId/bundleId, so re-processing is comparable even with a nondeterministic provider.

capabilities.label: TemporalFrame
capabilities.description: Distinguishes documentCreatedAt / documentReceivedAt / eventTime / effectiveTime / knownAt / extractedAt; knownAt is bounded by artifact receipt and can never postdate extraction (assertFrameCoherent). Document-stated times keep their written precision with no fabricated year, zone or midnight instant.

capabilities.label: Typed Refusal / Absence vocabulary
capabilities.description: Whole-operation failures are Refusal {code (OCR_FAILED, DOCUMENT_UNREADABLE, CLASSIFICATION_UNCERTAIN, CONFLICT_DETECTED, PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE, UNSUPPORTED_MIME, FIELD_NOT_FOUND, CANONICAL_STATE_BREACH ...), detail, remedy, stage, artifactIds}; field-level absence is a typed Absence with reason. null never stands where the reason for absence matters. Result<T> = ok | refusal is the return type of every tool and provider method.

capabilities.label: npm run demo (rate confirmation -> operator surface)
capabilities.description: Milestone demo: fixture provider offline by default (deterministic); with --live path/to/ratecon.pdf and MISTRAL_API_KEY it sends a real PDF to the Mistral OCR API and prints shipment observations with confidence, status, evidence locations and entity candidates. The live path spends external API calls and transmits document content to a third party.

capabilities.label: npm test / typecheck / audit:boundary (offline)
capabilities.description: vitest suite over the fixture corpus incl. adversarial shapes; npm run audit:boundary runs only the canonical-state boundary audit (source-tree walk + guard tests); npm run typecheck runs tsc --noEmit. Deterministic, no network, no secrets.

capabilities.label: npm run test:live (opt-in Mistral integration)
capabilities.description: RUN_LIVE_TESTS=1 vitest run: exercises MistralOCRProvider against the real Mistral API (requires MISTRAL_API_KEY); external calls and spend.

metadata.ocr_provider: mistral (behind OCRModel seam); fixture provider for tests
metadata.document_types: RATE_CONFIRMATION, BILL_OF_LADING, PROOF_OF_DELIVERY, INVOICE (+10 classify-only types)
metadata.data_domains: automation canonical-state evidence-pool identity model-weights network-health ontology security-posture trade-documents

nodes.name: Payload Earth (Payload Render Engine)
nodes.description: PAYLOAD EARTH is the cinematic WebGL/Three.js globe digital twin of the physical economy: ports, airports, rail terminals, warehouses, mines, refineries, chokepoints and cities drawn as nodes; road/rail/maritime/air routes as first-class semantic objects; commodity flows animated as GPU particle streams; a sim clock that scrubs historical/current/forecast state; and an inspector that shows promises (Assertions) against evidence (Observations) with computed Deviations. It is a strict projection of Payload state: it never owns or mutates canonical state, and it must never become a simulator or a second representation of state next to the Payload Terminal. Today every record is synthetic (provenance.source 'synthetic:demo', built in-process by src/data/synthetic/world.ts); no network fetch to Payload Terminal exists yet - the SpatialDataProvider seam (load/stateAt/query/subscribe) is where a Payload Spatial API client plugs in. Basemap geometry is static world-atlas TopoJSON shipped under public/data/.

capabilities.label: Interactive globe world view
capabilities.description: Principal UI: procedural day/night Earth (Natural Earth 50m land topology + corpus city lights), atmosphere, graticule, starfield; drag to rotate, wheel to zoom with altitude-driven LOD/progressive disclosure gated by Entity.importance. Nodes, per-mode route polylines and flow particles are drawn from the WorldSnapshot only.

capabilities.label: Command bar (text grammar over AppApi)
capabilities.description: Forgiving command grammar: find/goto <name>, show/hide <layer|group>, show <commodity> flows, flows on/off, play/pause/now, speed 1h|6h|24h, compare <a> vs <b>, view presets (world/freight/trade/commodities/network/exceptions), follow the load, help. Pure functions executeCommand/suggestCommands with autocomplete suggestions. All verbs are view operations on the projection.

capabilities.label: Layer panel (22 layers in 5 groups)
capabilities.description: Toggle layer visibility across WORLD (countries, cities, terrain, nightlights), TRANSPORT (road, rail, maritime, air), INFRASTRUCTURE (ports, airports, rail_terminals, warehouses, industrial), ECONOMY (production, demand, inventory, flows) and INTELLIGENCE (bottlenecks, constraints, anomalies, dependencies, risk). Kept in sync via layersChange events.

capabilities.label: Entity inspector (promises vs evidence)
capabilities.description: Info panel for a selected facility, route or flow: identity, provenance source, status, capacity, connected routes/flows, active events and constraints, and for routes the PROMISED transit (Assertion) against OBSERVED transits (Observations, n=) with the computed Deviation and a utilization sparkline. Reads provenance.source on the record; never replaces it.

capabilities.label: Timeline scrubber and playback
capabilities.description: Global sim-time control bound to the snapshot timeRange {start,end,now}: scrub, play/pause, speed; regime shown as historical / current (within +/-30 min of dataset now) / forecast ('scenario' reserved). Every dynamic layer resolves state deterministically via store.stateAt(entityId, simTime).

capabilities.label: Status bar with provenance chip
capabilities.description: Persistent HUD showing fps, camera altitude (km), visible nodes/routes, particle count, sim time/regime, and the SYNTHETIC / DEMO DATA disclaimer chip read from snapshot.meta.disclaimer.

capabilities.label: Country selection and summary
capabilities.description: Click a country (point-in-polygon on Natural Earth 110m borders) to select it and open a summary: nodes in country, routes touching it, flows, and route counts per transport mode (CountryInfo).

capabilities.label: Compare two routes
capabilities.description: compare <a> vs <b>: side-by-side great-circle distance, promised duration (assertion of record) and live utilization at the current sim time for two searched routes. Distances are presented as great-circle estimates, never road distance.

capabilities.label: Follow the Load cinematic scenario
capabilities.description: Scripted multimodal demo (GTA West DC -> Toronto intermodal -> Hwy 401 -> Windsor-Detroit Ambassador Bridge -> I-94 -> Chicago DC): camera dolly along the path with step captions. A long-running view operation on the mirror; 'stop'/Escape exits. No state is changed.

capabilities.label: Tool: fly_to (lat, lon, altitude)
capabilities.description: Structured agent tool exposed at window.payloadEarth.invokeTool('fly_to', {lat, lon, altitude?}): smoothly flies the camera to a WGS84 point at an optional altitude in earth radii. Safety flags destructive/longRunning/requiresConfirmation all false.

capabilities.label: Tool: find (fuzzy entity search + focus)
capabilities.description: invokeTool('find', {query}): scored fuzzy search over nodes, routes and flows by name; returns SearchResult[] {id, name, kind, score, detail} and cinematically focuses the best match.

capabilities.label: Tool: select_entity by id
capabilities.description: invokeTool('select_entity', {id}): selects an entity id (e.g. node:port-shanghai, route:..., flow:...) and opens the inspector; emits a select event with source 'command'.

capabilities.label: Tool: set_layer visibility
capabilities.description: invokeTool('set_layer', {layer, visible}): toggles one LayerId (e.g. transport.maritime, intel.bottlenecks).

capabilities.label: Tool: set_preset view preset
capabilities.description: invokeTool('set_preset', {preset}): applies a curated layer combination - world, freight, trade, commodities, network or exceptions.

capabilities.label: Tool: set_flow_mode particles on/off
capabilities.description: invokeTool('set_flow_mode', {enabled}): enables/disables the GPU flow-particle layer (particle density proportional to Flow.intensity; particles are representational, not real shipments).

capabilities.label: Tool: set_time (scrub fraction)
capabilities.description: invokeTool('set_time', {fraction}): scrubs sim time to a 0..1 fraction of the snapshot timeRange; deterministic re-render.

capabilities.label: Tool: set_playing (play/pause)
capabilities.description: invokeTool('set_playing', {playing}): plays or pauses the sim clock (default 3600 sim-seconds per wall-second).

capabilities.label: Tool: run_command (command-bar string)
capabilities.description: invokeTool('run_command', {command}): executes any command-bar string and returns CommandResult {ok, message}.

capabilities.label: Tool: get_state (twin view state snapshot)
capabilities.description: invokeTool('get_state'): returns {time: TemporalState, selection, country, preset, flowMode, layers: LayerDef[], data: snapshot.meta {label, disclaimer, generatedAt}} - the machine-readable view state incl. the data disclaimer.

capabilities.label: Tool: follow_the_load (long-running demo)
capabilities.description: invokeTool('follow_the_load'): starts the Toronto -> Chicago cinematic multimodal scenario; flagged longRunning: true, not destructive.

capabilities.label: AppApi facade (window.payloadEarth.api)
capabilities.description: The single typed facade all UI and agent bindings use: events bus, store, clock, camera (flyToLatLon, frameRoute, followPath, altitudeRadii), layer/preset/flow-mode getters and setters, select/focus/selectCountry/countryInfo, runCommand/suggest/search, demo start/stop. Exposed at runtime as window.payloadEarth.api.

capabilities.label: WorldStore read-only query API
capabilities.description: Indexed, renderer-blind read API over the snapshot: node/route/flow/commodity/entity by id, routesOfNode, flowsThroughRoute, flowsTouchingNode, routesByMode, nodesInCountry, routesTouchingCountry, stateAt(entityId,t), activeEvents(t), deviationsFor(entityId) (on-demand assertion/observation join), search(q). Never mutates.

capabilities.label: Typed AppEvents stream
capabilities.description: EventBus<AppEvents> that UI, layers and bindings subscribe to: select, hover, countrySelect, layersChange, time (TemporalState), preset, flowMode, demo (step/caption), toast, status (fps/altitude/visible counts/particles).

capabilities.label: SpatialDataProvider seam (ingress contract)
capabilities.description: The only data interface the twin consumes: load(): Promise<WorldSnapshot> (mandatory hydration), stateAt(entityId, t): EntityState (mandatory, deterministic), optional query(ViewportQuery{bbox, altitude, minImportance}) for PostGIS/vector-tile window queries, optional subscribe(onDelta) for push deltas from canonical state. A Payload Spatial API client implements this without touching the renderer.

capabilities.label: WorldSnapshot schema
capabilities.description: What a provider hands the renderer: nodes: Facility[], routes: Route[], flows: Flow[], commodities, events: WorldEvent[], constraints, assertions, observations, cityLights [lon,lat,intensity][], timeRange {start,end,now}, meta {label, disclaimer, generatedAt}. WGS84 lon/lat, GeoJSON-compatible Point/LineString geometry.

capabilities.label: Facility / NodeKind ontology
capabilities.description: Entity base (id, kind, name, geometry, status LifecycleStatus incl. 'unknown', provenance, importance 0..1, country ISO-2, tags) and Facility (inputs/outputs commodity ids, capacity QuantityRating, operator, connectedRouteIds) with subtypes Port (portType container|bulk|energy|mixed, berths, drafts), Airport (iata, cargoTonnesPerYear), RailTerminal (intermodal), Warehouse (areaSqm). NodeKind covers logistics, extraction, processing, industry, city and chokepoint.

capabilities.label: Route, TransportSegment, Commodity and Flow schema
capabilities.description: Route: mode road|rail|maritime|air, LineString geometry, originId/destinationId, distanceKm, estimatedDurationHours, capacity, utilization, constraints (chokepoint/border/capacity/draft_limit/weather/regulatory/congestion with atFraction), historicalState samples, corridorId, geometryBasis routed|great_circle_estimate|synthetic_corridor. Flow: commodityId, origin/destination, ordered TransportSegments (routeId, span), intensity 0..1, status moving|holding|delayed|delivered.

capabilities.label: Provenance block (is-this-real as a query)
capabilities.description: Every world-describing record carries Provenance {source: DataSource ('synthetic:demo' | 'payload:canonical' | 'payload:spatial' | 'external:osm' | 'external:ais' | 'external:gov-gis' | string), knownAt, validFrom?, validTo?, evidence?: string[], confidence?}. The build fails if any record lacks provenance.source.

capabilities.label: Assertion / Observation / Deviation model
capabilities.description: Promises and evidence are distinct records: Assertion {entityId, metric, value, unit, assertedAt, provenance}, Observation {entityId, t, metric, value, provenance}, Deviation {assertionId, observationId, delta = observed - asserted, ratio}. Route.estimatedDurationHours/capacity are projections of the current assertion and are never overwritten by outcomes.

capabilities.label: WorldEvent and Constraint schema
capabilities.description: WorldEvent {affects: EntityId[], severity, start, end?, category congestion|closure|weather|strike|demand_surge|incident, provenance} perturbs entity state through smooth ramps; Constraint attaches a standing typed constraint with validity window to an entity.

capabilities.label: TemporalState / EntityState
capabilities.description: TemporalState {t, regime historical|current|forecast|scenario, referenceNow, scenarioId?} fans out on the event bus; EntityState {entityId, t, utilization, congestion, status, activeEventIds} is the deterministic per-entity dynamic state a provider resolves for (entityId, t).

capabilities.label: Synthetic demo world v1 dataset
capabilities.description: In-process SyntheticProvider ('Synthetic demo world v1'): 114 nodes (26 ports incl. Shanghai, Singapore, Rotterdam, LA/Long Beach; 16 cargo airports; 10 rail terminals; DCs; Windsor-Detroit border crossing; mines, oil fields, agri belts, steel mills, refineries; 8 chokepoints - Panama, Suez, Malacca, Hormuz, Gibraltar, Bab el-Mandeb, Bosporus, Dover; 12 cities), 55 routes over 9 corridors, 16 commodities with derived flows, events, constraints, assertions and observations. Dynamic state is a hash-seeded pure function of (entityId, t). Every record has provenance.source 'synthetic:demo'.

capabilities.label: Static basemap assets (world-atlas TopoJSON)
capabilities.description: Served static files fetched by the client at boot: public/data/land-50m.json (Natural Earth 50m land, used to generate procedural day/night/mask textures) and public/data/countries-110m.json (borders + point-in-polygon country picking). No external imagery or tile servers.

capabilities.label: npm run check (seam + provenance + types)
capabilities.description: Validation gate run before every build: scripts/check-seam.mjs (src/data/** imports no packages and never escapes the data layer except core/events.ts and core/time.ts), scripts/validate-provenance.mjs (executes buildWorldSnapshot() and fails on any node/route/flow/commodity/event/constraint/assertion/observation lacking provenance.source), and tsc --noEmit strict.

capabilities.label: Vite dev server / production build / preview
capabilities.description: npm run dev (Vite dev server, host: true), npm run build (runs check, then vite build to dist/ with base './' so the twin deploys as a static site), npm run preview. Build is a local compute job producing the deployable static bundle.

nodes.name: Payload Terminal V0
nodes.description: Payload Supply Chain Management, the physical-commerce operating system: a Next.js 16 terminal that holds a provenance-preserving world state for commodities (copper, aluminium) and freight (loads, lanes, carriers, commitments) in which every figure carries source, basis and the date it became knowable, and an unanswerable question returns a typed refusal (value null + refusalType + remedy) instead of a zero. It is the operator surface of the Payload ecosystem: HTTP projections under /api/economy and /api/freight, a stdio MCP server of 12 read-only tools that call those same routes, conditional OSINT attribution routes, and append-only hash-chained freight journals. Machine clients send x-payload-client: machine (legacy x-sea-dog-client) and are served identically but segregated from the frozen researcher demand instruments into data-archive/mcp-sessions.jsonl. It must never become a person-intelligence tool (username, breach, phone and scanning capabilities were deleted, and CI gates every route), never turn a refusal into a zero, and never accept an export back into state.

capabilities.label: Physical-economy projections (map/analytics/timeline/graph/state)
capabilities.description: GET /api/economy?commodity=copper|aluminium&view=map|analytics|timeline|graph|state. map: entities and flows with disruption flags at the evaluation date; analytics: concentration (HHI with partition), centrality, bottlenecks, anomalies, propagation, corpusHealth, sources; timeline: playback range; graph: force-graph projection; state: full canonical state. Accepts asOf=YYYY-MM-DD and knowledge=best_known|as_known_then (as_known_then withholds and counts records not knowable at asOf). Unanswerable questions return typed refusals (value null + refusalType + remedy), never a zero.

capabilities.label: Entity inspector
capabilities.description: GET /api/economy/entity?commodity=&id=ent:... returns one entity's canonical state: observations with unit/basis/valueKind/source/knownAt, capacities, flows in/out, events, and resolved upstream/downstream chains so a client never owns graph logic. Accepts asOf=YYYY-MM-DD and knowledge=best_known|as_known_then (as_known_then withholds and counts records not knowable at asOf).

capabilities.label: Entity and evidence search
capabilities.description: GET /api/economy/search?q= searches the canonical register (mines, smelters, refineries, ports, companies, countries) by name, operator, country or kind; the index IS the register. Queries whose first token names an epistemic state (refused[:type], stale[:type], contested[:class], vintage) search the evidence layer instead. A true miss names registered-but-unbuilt sources (registryGaps). Accepts asOf=YYYY-MM-DD and knowledge=best_known|as_known_then (as_known_then withholds and counts records not knowable at asOf).

capabilities.label: Corpus table and period x edition grid
capabilities.description: GET /api/economy/table?commodity=[&metric=&subject=&format=json|md] renders the corpus as rows carrying record_id, the five axes, source, period, known_at, attestation and a server-rendered claim sentence; refused subjects are null-valued rows with a remedy. view=grid&subject=&metric= returns the period x edition grid (null cell = not covered, never zero). GET-only by design; CSV/XLSX refused. Exports are logged to data-archive/export-log.jsonl. Accepts asOf=YYYY-MM-DD and knowledge=best_known|as_known_then (as_known_then withholds and counts records not knowable at asOf).

capabilities.label: Refusals digest and session telemetry
capabilities.description: GET /api/economy/refusals?commodity=[&asOf=&knowledge=] returns everything the instrument declined to answer, grouped by refusal type with the type's shared remedy, most-blocking mechanism first: a work queue. ?view=session returns the session telemetry digest (queries, misses, withheld, exports) with no query strings and no personal data.

capabilities.label: Runtime guard evaluation and build identity
capabilities.description: GET /api/economy/guards[?now=YYYY-MM-DD] evaluates the validWhile guards of every deferred ledger decision against the state this instance is actually serving (not CI's verdict on the repository) and reports version.commit / commit_source (unstamped-build when PAYLOAD_BUILD_SHA is absent). Used as the S-6 session baseline capture.

capabilities.label: Claim validator as a service
capabilities.description: GET /api/economy/validate?claim=...&records=obs:a,obs:b[&commodity=&asOf=&knowledge=] judges the support relation between a natural-language claim (from any model) and the records it cites. Verdicts: supported, partially_supported, unsupported, overstated, inadmissible (rests on representative-attested input). Never recomputes analytics, never supplies uncited evidence; the claim text is never logged.

capabilities.label: Counterfactual scenario injection
capabilities.description: POST /api/economy/scenario {commodity?, asOf?, knowledge?, label, events[]} runs the propagation engine twice on the same frame (reconstruction and with hypothetical events injected) and returns both plus the delta on an explicit counterfactual frame. Nothing is written; the scenario exists only in the response.

capabilities.label: Entity expansion via the OSIRIS intel layer
capabilities.description: GET /api/entity/expand?type=aircraft|vessel|company|person|ip|country&id=[&registration&model&icao24] validates the request and forwards it to the osiris-intel service (INTEL_URL, default http://payload-intel:4000 in production) returning its {nodes, links} ontology graph. Rate-limited 30/min per client IP; response cached 1h.

capabilities.label: Read load-operation projections
capabilities.description: GET /api/freight/operations[?operationId=] lists or reads the replayable load-operation projections (opportunity intake, alternatives, authorization, assignment, dispatch, outcome) derived from the append-only hash-chained operations journal (PAYLOAD_OPERATIONS_LOG). Requires Authorization: Bearer PAYLOAD_OPERATIONS_TOKEN; fail-closed (503) when the token is unset.

capabilities.label: Advance a load operation (typed commands)
capabilities.description: POST /api/freight/operations {command, payload} appends to the operations journal. Commands: register_opportunity, register_alternative, authorize_alternative, open_episode, record_assignment, explore_assignment, dispatch, capture_outcome, capture_settlement. 201 on append, 200 on idempotent replay, 409 on phase/id conflicts, 422 on typed refusals, 413 above 1 MB (raw documents do not belong in the journal). Requires Authorization: Bearer PAYLOAD_OPERATIONS_TOKEN; fail-closed (503) when the token is unset.

capabilities.label: Control-tower read model
capabilities.description: GET /api/freight/control-tower joins the operations and carrier-communication journals into an exception-first desk queue: load/carrier/lane/episode identity, authorization through settlement state, pickup/delivery commitments, tracking freshness, quoted cost, invoice, margin. Every item names an issue, severity, deadline, evidence count and operator remedy; no composite score. Journal corruption makes the whole view refuse rather than show an empty desk. Requires Authorization: Bearer PAYLOAD_OPERATIONS_TOKEN; fail-closed (503) when the token is unset.

capabilities.label: Read carrier-communication projections
capabilities.description: GET /api/freight/communications[?operationId=] exposes tender delivery attempts, receipts and carrier-event projections from the carrier-communications journal (PAYLOAD_CARRIER_COMMUNICATIONS_LOG). Requires Authorization: Bearer PAYLOAD_OPERATIONS_TOKEN; fail-closed (503) when the token is unset.

capabilities.label: Deliver a tender to the carrier adapter
capabilities.description: POST /api/freight/communications {command:"send_dispatch", payload} delivers the journal-derived tender to the configured outbound carrier adapter (PAYLOAD_CARRIER_DISPATCH_URL, bearer PAYLOAD_CARRIER_DISPATCH_TOKEN) with a stable Idempotency-Key, at-least-once across a crash. The carrier receives only the selected rate and sanitized load facts, never the shipper target rate. 503 carrier_gateway_not_configured when the adapter is unset. Requires Authorization: Bearer PAYLOAD_OPERATIONS_TOKEN; fail-closed (503) when the token is unset.

capabilities.label: Inbound carrier acknowledgement/tracking webhook
capabilities.description: POST /api/freight/carrier-events records carrier acknowledgements and tracking updates into the communications journal. Authenticated by x-payload-timestamp and x-payload-signature = sha256=HMAC-SHA256(timestamp + "." + rawBody) under PAYLOAD_CARRIER_WEBHOOK_SECRET (>= 32 bytes; 300 s skew; 256 KB cap). Events bind to immutable dispatch identities; orphan or mismatched histories are refused.

capabilities.label: Authoritative carrier and diesel evidence pull-through
capabilities.description: GET /api/freight/sources?usdot=&carrierId=[&includeDiesel=1] pulls FMCSA QCMobile identity/authority/out-of-service evidence and the fixed EIA weekly U.S. diesel benchmark (FMCSA_WEB_KEY, EIA_API_KEY). Returns a gate-ready authorizationCarrier with insurance expiry and cargo cover deliberately null; excludes carrier address/telephone; partial upstream failure is a typed source refusal, never a stale value or inferred pass. Requires Authorization: Bearer PAYLOAD_OPERATIONS_TOKEN; fail-closed (503) when the token is unset.

capabilities.label: End-to-end freight run over the simulated backend
capabilities.description: GET /api/freight/demo[?format=text&now=ISO] runs nine hand-built loads through the notary, lifecycle engine and spatial abstraction and pins every refusal. The clock is a query parameter defaulted to the fixture instant so two responses can be diffed.

capabilities.label: Detector discrimination run over a generated freight world
capabilities.description: GET /api/freight/world?now=ISO&seed=int generates a ~520-load population with planted signals and reports whether each detector (lane residuals, carrier vetting, exception queue) found what the world manifest says it planted. Same seed, byte-identical world.

capabilities.label: WHOIS/RDAP domain attribution
capabilities.description: GET /api/osint/whois resolves a domain's registrant organisation via RDAP and cross-checks registrant/org names against the OFAC SDN list (OpenSanctions mirror), surfacing an inline alert. CONDITIONAL under the collection policy: organisational infrastructure attribution only; never used to profile, locate or identify a natural person, and the constraint is stated in the route source.

capabilities.label: DNS lookup (DoH)
capabilities.description: GET /api/osint/dns resolves records for a domain via Google DNS-over-HTTPS. CONDITIONAL under the collection policy: organisational infrastructure attribution only; never used to profile, locate or identify a natural person, and the constraint is stated in the route source.

capabilities.label: IP geolocation, ASN and OFAC screening of the announcing org
capabilities.description: GET /api/osint/ip returns geolocation, reputation and ASN owner for an address block and screens the ASN owner against the OFAC SDN list. nodes.name: PYTHIA Oracle Engine
nodes.description: A FastAPI forecasting oracle ("Osiris world data in, future predictions out") found in engine/ of the Payload-Terminal-V0 repository as Python 3.14 bytecode only, with its ledger in runs/ledger.jsonl. It reads the terminal's public /api/* feeds (OSIRIS_URL) into a prose world brief, asks a local OpenAI-compatible LLM (Ollama by default, no cloud) for concrete predictions per horizon, optionally has a swarm council of persona agents deliberate and weight votes by their resolved Brier scores, persists every forecast to an append-only ledger, and later LLM-judges each forecast against the archived world to keep a scorecard. It exposes SSE and agent views for other agents and pushes outbound webhooks above probability/salience thresholds. It is a prototype whose source is not committed and whose intake targets routes the terminal has since retired; it must never be treated as canonical state or as validated risk, and its forecasts should be catalogued as proposals until the source and the intake are restored.

nodes.name: Scientific Compute Layer (SCL)
nodes.description: A reusable native scientific-computation layer in C++17/CUDA behind a process boundary: scl_cli reads one JSON request from stdin, dispatches on the operation field through a fixed registry (lj_pairwise_energy_forces, fourier_transform_1d, least_squares, kalman_filter_linear), and writes one JSON result to stdout with a staged fault vocabulary that is never collapsed to a generic failure. A dependency-free Python client (scl) encodes requests, drives the binary and content-addresses requests and results; a separate, explicitly imported scl.ste_adapter translates STE's ExecutionSpecification/ExecutionResult so SCL can be plugged in as a runner at STE's SpecificationDispatcher seam. SCL also holds its half of the requirement/capability exchange with the acquisition layer (DAQ). It is one integration environment for STE, not defined by it; it never admits evidence, never touches STE's Rust workspace, and never claims that a computation is a measurement. The CUDA backend compiles and links but has never executed on a GPU in any session.

capabilities.label: scl_cli request: one JSON object on stdin
capabilities.description: Request {operation, backend: cpu|cuda, configuration_hex, input_hex}. The envelope, hex framing and backend-availability check are operation-agnostic; the operation owns decoding, validation and dispatch. One process per computation. A request naming an unknown operation or backend is answered as halted with exit_code 10 (PROTOCOL); an unavailable backend halts with 12 before any bytes are decoded.

capabilities.label: scl_cli result: one JSON object on stdout
capabilities.description: Response {status: completed|halted, exit_code, backend_used, backend_version ('scl-cli/0.1.0'), output_hex (null when halted), detail (null when completed), metrics{...}} such as native_compute_seconds and n_particles. Process exit code is 0 whenever a well-formed JSON answer was produced, including halted; a non-zero process exit means the CLI could not answer at all.

capabilities.label: Staged fault codes
capabilities.description: exit_code 0 completed; 10 PROTOCOL (malformed envelope, unknown operation); 11 VALIDATION (bad parameters/input); 12 BACKEND_UNAVAILABLE (cuda without toolkit or device); 13 COMPUTATION (coincident particles, non-finite result); 14 INTERNAL (unexpected exception). Single source of truth in protocol.hpp, mirrored in python/scl/errors.py and ste_adapter FAULT_* constants.

capabilities.label: Report the native binary version
capabilities.description: scl_cli --version prints the kernel version string (scl-cli/0.1.0), the same value echoed as backend_version in every response and folded into STE's program bytes by the adapter, so a kernel version bump is a new program identity.

capabilities.label: CUDA backend selection
capabilities.description: backend 'cuda' routes lj_pairwise and fourier (cuFFT) to native/backends/cuda when built with -DSCL_WITH_CUDA=ON and a device is visible; otherwise halts with 12. Implemented, compiled and linked against CUDA 12, 51/51 native tests, but never GPU-executed in any session (cudaGetDeviceCount()==0); CPU-CUDA equivalence, determinism and performance are explicitly not claimed.

capabilities.label: Compute truncated Lennard-Jones energy and forces
capabilities.description: operation 'lj_pairwise_energy_forces': configuration 24 bytes = epsilon, sigma, cutoff as f64 LE; input N*24 bytes of (x,y,z) f64 LE; output 8 + N*24 bytes = total_energy then per-particle (fx,fy,fz). V(r)=4eps[(s/r)^12-(s/r)^6] for r<=cutoff, plain truncation. Faults: sigma/epsilon/cutoff not finite or <=0 (11), zero particles (11), coincident particles (13). Bitwise reproducible on the same binary and machine.

capabilities.label: Compute the 1-D discrete Fourier transform
capabilities.description: operation 'fourier_transform_1d': configuration 24 bytes = int32 direction(+1 forward|-1 inverse), int32 normalization(0 none|1 1/N|2 1/sqrt N), int32 has_sample_spacing, int32 reserved=0, f64 sample_spacing_seconds; input N*16 bytes complex (re,im) f64; output N complex bins k=0..N-1, no fftshift. Any N>=1; CPU evaluates the O(N^2) defining sum. Spacing bytes under has_sample_spacing=0 are refused, never ignored.

capabilities.label: Solve a (weighted) linear least-squares fit
capabilities.description: operation 'least_squares': configuration = int32 weighted, three int32 zeros, f64 rank_tolerance (relative singular-value cutoff, explicit at every call site); input = int32 n_rows, int32 n_cols, X row-major f64, y f64, optional per-row weights f64; output = coefficient vector f64 LE. Weights are inputs, not parameters, so parameters_identity stays comparable across datasets. Row order is not significant.

capabilities.label: Run a linear Kalman filter over a measurement stream
capabilities.description: operation 'kalman_filter_linear': configuration = int32 n, m, Q provenance (always ASSERTED=0), R provenance (0 asserted|1 supplied), two reserved, f64 symmetry_tolerance, psd_tolerance, then F(n*n), H(m*n), Q(n*n), R(m*m) f64; input = int32 steps, int32 source_identity_length, x0, P0, measurements (ordered), source identity bytes. supplied on Q, or a source identity under asserted R, is a validation fault. Order of measurements is significant.

capabilities.label: Drive scl_cli from Python
capabilities.description: run_scl_request(SCLRequest, cli_path=default_cli_path(), timeout=60.0) -> SCLResult. Spawns one scl_cli process, marshals JSON, decodes output bytes. Raises SCLProtocolError (missing binary, unparseable stdout, non-zero process exit) or SCLTimeoutError for channel failures; a halted computation is returned as a normal SCLResult, convertible to a typed exception with raise_for_result.

capabilities.label: Content-addressed request and result identities
capabilities.description: SCLRequest exposes operation_identity, parameters_identity, input_identity and identity(); SCLResult exposes output_identity and computation_identity. Scheme: length-prefixed tag + fields, SHA-256, lowercase hex under scl.request.*.v1 / scl.result.*.v1 domain tags, a separate namespace from STE's scout.execution.* identities. Annotating parameters (e.g. sample spacing) change request identity but not computation identity.

capabilities.label: Encode/decode Lennard-Jones wire payloads
capabilities.description: encode_lj_configuration(epsilon, sigma, cutoff), encode_lj_positions(positions), decode_lj_configuration(bytes) and decode_lj_output(bytes) -> (total_energy, forces) produce and read exactly the byte layout scl_cli expects (little-endian float64).

capabilities.label: Encode/decode Fourier payloads and derive the frequency axis
capabilities.description: encode_fourier_configuration, decode_fourier_configuration, encode_complex_signal, encode_real_signal, decode_complex_spectrum, frequency_bins(n, sample_spacing) (returns None with no spacing; never assumes dt=1) and spectral_power_total; constants FORWARD/INVERSE and NORMALIZATION_NONE/ONE_OVER_N/ONE_OVER_SQRT_N.

capabilities.label: Encode/decode least-squares payloads and residuals
capabilities.description: encode_least_squares_configuration(rank_tolerance, weighted), encode_least_squares_input(design, response, weights), decode_least_squares_output, residuals and normal_equation_residual helpers for independent checking of a returned fit.

capabilities.label: Encode Kalman configuration and input
capabilities.description: encode_kalman_configuration(F, H, Q, R, measurement_noise_provenance=ASSERTED, symmetry_tolerance, psd_tolerance) and encode_kalman_input(x0, P0, measurements, source_identity=None). There is deliberately no process-noise provenance argument: Q is always asserted.

capabilities.label: Typed Quantity with explicit uncertainty kind
capabilities.description: Quantity(value, unit, uncertainty_kind in stated|estimated|propagated|absent, uncertainty) and absent_uncertainty(value, unit): a JSON-serializable shape for values placed inside STE's open Observation.content, not a second evidence system.

capabilities.label: Domain method blocks for computed results
capabilities.description: LJMethodBlock / lj_method_block_for and FourierMethodBlock / fourier_method_block_for record what was computed (potential form, cutoff handling, algorithm, normalization, frequency-axis applicability) with every non-applicable field marked applicable: false and a reason, never omitted or fabricated.

capabilities.description:
run_scl_specification(spec, cli_path, timeout) is a drop-in runner for STE's SpecificationDispatcher (alternative to execution.gromacs). It splits the program descriptor 'ste.scl.<operation>.v1
<version line>
[backend]
<cpu|cuda>', runs scl_cli, recomputes output_identity and computation_identity with execution.commitments from bytes it holds, and returns STE's ExecutionResult with the same FAULT_* codes. Only this module imports STE.

capabilities.label: Build an STE specification for an SCL operation

capabilities.label: Interpret an SCL ExecutionResult as evidence-classed content

SCL never calls admission itself.

capabilities.label: Participating, annotating and provenance parameter rules
capabilities.description: Every configuration field is participating (read by the mathematics; enters output and computation identity) or annotating (enters request identity only, e.g. sample spacing); noise matrices additionally carry a supplied|asserted provenance discriminant that participates. A guarded payload must have exactly one encoding per meaning and is refused when unused. Enforced registry-wide by tests/test_annotating_parameters.py and test_operation_registry_contract.py.

capabilities.label: Scoped reproducibility claims

Not claimed: physical correspondence to a measurement, cross-machine or cross-compiler bitwise equality, CPU-CUDA agreement.
