nodes.name: Scientific Transformer Engine (Deterministic State Architecture)
nodes.description: The canonical-state compiler pipeline of the scientific vertical: a single versioned, immutable CanonicalState is the sole source of truth, validate_candidate is the only door to a new Version, and every Morpho IR document, Three.js scene, SVG diagram, graph metric, simulation or neural candidate downstream is a pure, deterministic projection that can never write state back. Around that core sit the SCOUT evidence pool and Trust Graph, a read-only retrieval engine, the materials/experiment decision layer and its workbench REPL, and the STE execution vertical: ExecutionSpecification -> a zero-dependency Rust execution-cli (checked, not trusted) or GROMACS -> DispatchedMeasurement -> evidence admission, optionally proved on SP1, Nexus or RISC Zero. It also declares core@1.0.0 and derives the cross-repository invariant register that binds the acquisition (DAQ) and compute (SCL) layers. It must never become a place where an inferred relation, a simulation candidate, or an execution transcript silently becomes canonical evidence, and it never claims that a computation is a measurement.

capabilities.label: CanonicalState data contract
capabilities.description: Frozen dataclass over an immutable mapping: schema_version, a map of Field(id, type, value, unit) whose id must equal its dictionary key, and a tuple of explicit EdgeRecord relationships (never inferred). Updating state always means producing a new CanonicalState; nothing in morpho/, backends/ or renderer/ may reach it.

capabilities.label: Version identity and VersionStore
capabilities.description: Version.id is a SHA-256 over (schema_version, fields, edges) only; id, parent, provenance and timestamp are excluded, so identical content yields identical ids across processes and PYTHONHASHSEED values. create_genesis_version is the only Version built outside validation; InMemoryVersionStore implements the VersionStore protocol.

capabilities.label: Diff two canonical states into a StateDelta
capabilities.description: diff(old, new, provenance) produces path-addressed leaf-level Changes (fields.mass.value, edges[0].type) with add/remove/replace operations in deterministic sorted order; apply_changes replays CandidateChanges onto a base state. Produces a delta for review; writes nothing canonical.

capabilities.label: Validate a candidate and mint a new Version
capabilities.description: The one door into a new version: candidate -> schema validation -> constraint validation -> accept -> new Version, or reject with ValidationErrors touching no state. validate_candidate is the only function in the codebase that can produce a new CanonicalState or Version; tests/test_architecture_boundaries.py enforces that no backend or renderer can reach it.

capabilities.label: Project a frozen Version into a ProjectedState
capabilities.description: project_state(version) and restore_projection(store, version_id, config) are pure functions from a frozen Version to the ProjectedState that the Morpho compiler consumes. Deterministic under replay (tests/test_replay.py).

capabilities.label: Compile a ProjectedState to Morpho IR
capabilities.description: compile_morpho(projected, CompilerConfig) -> MorphoDocument: the domain-neutral intermediate representation of entities, relations, coordinate frames, groups and constraints, each with explicit provenance. Every MorphoRelation carries is_canonical and inference_status; constructing one that is both canonical and inferred raises.

capabilities.label: Parse Morpho HDL text
capabilities.description: Lexer and parser for the human-readable Morpho HDL grammar (ARCHITECTURE_SPEC section 7 as corrected by docs/CONTRADICTIONS.md) producing the AST in morpho/ast.py; identity functions node_id/cell_id/visual_id/geometry_id are the identity on field_name in v1.

capabilities.label: Compile Morpho IR to a Three.js scene descriptor
capabilities.description: compile_threejs(ir, ThreeJSRenderConfig) returns a plain JSON-serializable ThreeJSSceneDescriptor (geometries, materials, meshes, hierarchy) keyed by geometry_id/visual_id so a renderer can update meshes in place. Never constructs a THREE.* object.

capabilities.label: Compile Morpho IR to an SVG document
capabilities.description: compile_svg(ir, DiagramLayoutConfig) returns a complete, deterministically laid-out SVG document string for the projected state.

capabilities.label: Descriptive graph metrics over Morpho IR
capabilities.description: analyze(ir) -> GraphAnalysisReport with node/edge counts, adjacency and degree over the relations the IR already contains; it never invents inferred relations.

capabilities.label: Simulation and neural interface shapes
capabilities.description: Protocol/dataclass shapes only (DynamicsSpec, Action, Observation, StructuredObservation, BeliefState, Estimator) per spec sections 16-17. No engine and no model are implemented; they define what a future simulation or estimator must return to enter the feedback loop.

capabilities.label: Submit a simulation candidate or neural belief toward canonical state
capabilities.description: submit_simulation_candidate / submit_neural_belief are the only bridge from a CandidateNextState or BeliefState back toward canonical state, and both hand the candidate to validate_candidate like a manual edit. No alternate fast path exists (runtime/test_feedback_loop.py).

capabilities.label: Three.js renderer page
capabilities.description: renderer/index.html fetches a ThreeJSSceneDescriptor JSON and renders it with vendored three.js, keeping a geometry_id/visual_id cache so value-only changes update meshes in place and deleted entities are removed. It has no code path back into canonical state.

capabilities.label: Generate demo scene descriptors
capabilities.description: python3 scripts/generate_sample_scene.py runs the full pipeline (CanonicalState -> validation -> projection -> Morpho -> Three.js backend) over a 10-field schema and writes demo ThreeJSSceneDescriptor JSON files for the renderer.

capabilities.label: Normalize external JSON to a CandidateDelta
capabilities.description: JSONAdapter and infer_schema_from_record turn arbitrary JSON (nested objects, arrays, units/timestamps when supplied, relationships) into ExternalRecords and a CandidateDelta at the adapters.interface boundary. Output is a candidate for validation, never canonical state.

capabilities.label: Normalize CSV rows to a CandidateDelta
capabilities.description: parse_csv_rows / CSVAdapter / build_candidate_from_rows normalize single-row and multi-row CSV onto the same CandidateChange boundary as the JSON adapter (docs/DATA_CAPABILITIES.md lists exactly what is supported).

capabilities.label: Admit documents, records, observations and referents into the EvidencePool
capabilities.description: admit_document / admit_record / admit_observation / admit_referent / admit_claimed_relationship / admit_derived_value / admit_derived_grounding return the admitted object or a list of AdmissionErrors. The pool is append-only and content-addressed (EvidencePool.fingerprint()); quarantine and provenance are enforced at admission.

capabilities.label: Build the Trust Graph and network metrics
capabilities.description: build_trust_graph derives a read-only TrustGraph view over referents and claimed relationships in the pool; evidence/metrics.py computes the SCOUT network metrics documented in docs/SCOUT_ARCHITECTURE.md.

capabilities.label: Run the SCOUT observation pipeline
capabilities.description: run_scout drives a SourceAdapter (RawDocument) through an Extractor (ExtractionCandidate with entities and relations) and admits the result into an EvidencePool, returning ScoutFindings and ScoutAdmissionFailures. Deterministic sources only; stops at evidence attachment, before any autonomous experimentation.

capabilities.label: Deterministic read-only retrieval over the evidence pool
capabilities.description: make_retrieval_query + DeterministicRetrievalEngine produce RetrievalResults and a ContextPackage via exact lookup, Trust Graph traversal and text-substring matching only (no embeddings, no vector search, no database). Never writes to evidence/ or core.canonical.

capabilities.label: Ingest chemistry documents through the content gate
capabilities.description: ingest_documents(adapter, extractor, pool, ...) runs molecule/crystal/substance payloads through chemistry_content_gate, which refuses violating payloads with per-invariant refusal codes (architecture/verticals/chemistry) before anything reaches the pool.

capabilities.label: ExecutionSpecification and canonical input encoders
capabilities.description: ExecutionSpecification(program, configuration, input_payload) with identity commit('scout.execution.specification.v1', ...) over exactly three fields (no timestamps, hosts or versions-as-metadata). encode_positions, encode_heat_input, encode_rg_input, encode_crystal_input and encode_attention_input are the one canonical byte encoding per kernel.

capabilities.label: Registered deterministic native kernels
capabilities.description: Five integer-exact kernels with self-describing program descriptors: scout.native.pairwise-energy-kernel.v1, heat-diffusion-kernel.v1, radius-of-gyration-kernel.v1, crystal-lattice-kernel.v1 and attention-kernel.v1 (hardmax). Each descriptor states input layout, bounds, arithmetic and fault codes; the registry is a fixed array with no dynamic loading.

capabilities.label: execution-cli stdin/stdout execution protocol
capabilities.description: One Rust process per request stream: stdin carries B>=1 requests of three u64-LE length-prefixed fields [program descriptor][configuration][input]; stdout answers each with an 'ste-execution-result v1' block (spec, program, input, occurrence, status completed|halted|unrunnable, exit_code, output hex, output_id, computation, detail). Process exit 0 = answered, 2 = protocol error and nothing ran.

capabilities.label: Run a specification through the checked engine
capabilities.description: run_specification / run_specifications spawn execution-cli, recompute every echoed identity (specification, program, input, output, computation) from bytes Python holds, and raise EngineIdentityMismatch on disagreement, ExecutionRefused for unrunnable requests, EngineProtocolError for a malformed stream. Returns ExecutionResult.

capabilities.label: Run a GROMACS workload as an execution
capabilities.description: run_gromacs_specification (grompp -> mdrun nsteps=0 -> energy), run_gromacs_trajectory_specification and run_gromacs_minimization_specification wrap an external gmx binary. program = version line + topology, configuration = .mdp, input = .gro; output bytes are gmx's own text verbatim. Declared, not checked: this layer computes all identities.

capabilities.label: Dispatch a candidate through the execution seam
capabilities.description: SpecificationDispatcher is an ActionDispatcher whose runner (default run_specification; alternatives GROMACS or an external layer such as SCL's ste_adapter) is substitutable below the seam. dispatch(candidate) returns a DispatchedMeasurement declaring extraction_method 'simulation:...' whose execution transcript rides in the Record, never in the Observation.

capabilities.label: Prove and independently verify an execution on a zkVM
capabilities.description: prove_and_verify / prove_and_verify_result / proved_runner run the native execution, then an SP1, Nexus or RISC Zero host binary to prove and verify it, returning a ProvedRun only when every commitment agrees; otherwise ProvedRunError. Guest ELFs must be registered in execution.guest_registry. A ProvedRun never claims a measurement occurred.

capabilities.label: Verify an existing proof artifact
capabilities.description: verify_existing_proof re-runs the backend verifier against a stored proof and its Expectation; export_verification_artifact writes the Stage 10 verification artifact so a third party can re-verify without the prover. Produces a validation; writes no evidence.

capabilities.label: zkVM host prove/verify line protocol
capabilities.description: sp1_host, the Nexus host and the RISC Zero host accept 'prove' and 'verify' subcommands and answer with the shared 'ste-host-result v1' line protocol, so execution.proving is backend-neutral. Fork revisions and toolchains are pinned in zk/recipes/*.recipe.

capabilities.label: Reproducibly rebuild zkVM guests and regenerate the registry
capabilities.description: python3 -m execution.build rebuilds every guest from its zk/recipes/*.recipe (backend, guest crate, target, toolchain identity, rustflags, source file digests), verifies the ELF sha256 against the recipe, and regenerates execution/guest_registry.py. verify_build lets a distrusting verifier re-derive an artifact identity from source.

capabilities.label: Run a verification campaign under a policy
capabilities.description: run_campaign executes CampaignPoints through one EvidencePool and one OperationTrace under a VerificationPolicy (lanes: routine Nexus, deterministic RISC Zero and SP1 samples, escalation), reusing WarrantRecords from the warrant cache and prefetching proofs in parallel. Returns a CampaignReport.

capabilities.label: Run an experiment step and admit its result
capabilities.description: run_experiment_step takes what a dispatcher returns, admits the Record into the pool, hands semantic facts to materials.results (the sole semantic write boundary) and records the OperationOccurrence in the operations ledger; a failed dispatch records FAILED and admits nothing.

capabilities.label: Analyze a material research programme
capabilities.description: analyze_program(pool, engine, query) answers a MaterialProgramQuery with formulation/process associations and property evidence drawn only from the pool via the retrieval engine; the wider materials/ package provides candidates, predictions, utility ranking and counterfactuals as read-only projections.

capabilities.label: Workbench REPL: inspect, decide, explore and review
capabilities.description: python -m workbench [--scenario file.json] launches the SCOUT retrieval workbench. Commands scenario, status, candidates, predict, inspect, decide, explain, select, explore <value>, branches, compare, timeline, thread, state, criterion, history and diagnostics render existing domain objects; UNDETERMINED is rendered literally and hypotheticals are double-ruled.

capabilities.label: Workbench REPL: admit an external result
capabilities.description: The 'observe <value> [unit]' command admits an externally supplied experimental result for the active candidate into the session's experiment state, advancing the real state trajectory. Recommendation is never action: only this command and 'select' change session state.

capabilities.label: Run the hardmax attention model through the engine
capabilities.description: AttentionModel (three content-addressed integer d x d matrices, ste.transformer.model.v1) forwards a TransformerRepresentation token matrix through scout.native.attention-kernel.v1 via the unchanged execution boundary, yielding a Prediction with explicit uncertainty_kind that is structurally not evidence. Batched forwards amortize process spawn.

capabilities.label: Project a molecule to typed transformer tokens
capabilities.description: molecule_representation(molecule) -> TransformerRepresentation (ste.transformer.representation.v1): typed tokens mass_amu, x_pm, y_pm, z_pm derived from a canonical structures.Molecule.

capabilities.label: Core and invariant declarations
capabilities.description: architecture/core.yaml declares core@1.0.0 (moves only under bend_protocol, never on release); invariants.yaml lists 26 enforceable core invariants with status and named enforcement; evidence_class.yaml, model_binding.yaml, transformer_contract.yaml and exchange/ste_invariant_declaration.yaml are the contracts sibling repositories extend.

capabilities.label: Check vertical contracts, core closure and doctrine currency
capabilities.description: check_vertical_contract(path), check_core_closure() and check_doctrine_current() verify that a vertical extends the declared core, that the core imports nothing vendor-specific, and that the generated doctrine matches its sources; core_version() refuses a declaration derived from packaging.

capabilities.label: Generate the vendor-free doctrine
capabilities.description: python3 -m architecture.doctrine_generator renders architecture/generated/doctrine from the YAML declarations within a budget (DoctrineBudgetError) and lints it vendor-free.

capabilities.label: Derive the cross-repository invariant register
capabilities.description: derive() reads the three bound repositories STE, DAQ (notations-acquisition-channel) and SCL (scientific-compute-layer), establishes provenance and remote currency per party, and emits architecture/exchange/invariant_register.yaml with a sha256 sidecar; build_invariant_register.py is the CLI. Fails closed on an unreachable or unbound party.

capabilities.label: Reachability probes for admission gates and invariants
capabilities.description: canonical_state_reachability.py, chemistry_reachability.py and ingest_reachability_probe.py plant violating payloads against each gate and report REACHABLE / DEAD / UNREACHED per invariant, so a clean rejection rate is never read as evidence that a gate is on the path. The mutate_* scripts probe the probes themselves.

capabilities.label: Stage 6-11 execution and proof campaigns
capabilities.description: stage6_campaign.py through stage11_campaign.py and structural_campaign.py run real heat-diffusion sweeps, molecular/crystal structures, GROMACS trajectories, policy-verified proofs (Nexus, RISC Zero, SP1), warrant reuse and parallel prefetch through one pool and one operation trace. Each spawns engines and provers and admits evidence.

capabilities.label: Engine and transformer benchmarks
capabilities.description: transformer_baseline.py, transformer_batch_bench.py, engine_request_profile.py and checker_profile.py measure per-forward, per-request and per-item costs of the execution boundary by differential measurement; they spawn engine processes but admit nothing.

nodes.name: TrustGraph
nodes.description: Mirror of trustgraph-ai/trustgraph, an open-source context interoperability layer: a Pulsar-backed processing platform that ingests documents, extracts entities and relationships with LLMs into an RDF/OWL hypergraph (N-Quads, named graphs), stores graph and document embeddings, and serves GraphRAG, DocumentRAG, SPARQL, GraphQL-over-rows, agent and prompt services through an API gateway (REST, WebSocket) and an MCP server. In the Notations Universe it is a candidate knowledge-graph substrate for corpus and archive nodes: workspaces, collections and portable knowledge cores are the units of context. It is an upstream mirror, not first-party code, and must not become the canonical state of the universe; the control plane journal remains authoritative.

capabilities.description: POST /api/v1/iam: whoami, list my workspaces, create/list/get/update/disable users, create/list workspaces, create/list/revoke API keys, admin password reset. Bearer tokens obtained here scope every other call to a workspace.

Confirmed by code and shared files: DAQ emits daq_capabilities.yaml and daq_requirement_response.yaml (content-addressed with the byte-identical canonical_yaml.py emitter) as its half of the two-artifact exchange with the Scientific Compute Layer, mirrors SCL's scl_requirements.yaml and scl_contract_clauses.yaml read-only, and the two repositories co-sign the 2026-08-26 joint workload decision (least_squares) that obliges DAQ to build the aligned observation table. verify_pair_landed.py checks the shared architecture/ subtree is byte-identical across both remotes.

Confirmed by code: DAQ is the acquisition stage of the STE control loop. Adapters produce RawDocuments that the vendored scout.pipeline.run_scout admits into an EvidencePool (DurablePool/ClassifiedPool subclasses), from which STE's materials ModelState, trust graph and retrieval derive; science/ reads materials' EvidenceRequirements and returns AcquisitionIntents as the loop's only exit from derived_state. DAQ never writes canonical state (system rule: STE promotes).

Only in the integrated configuration: scl.ste_adapter imports execution.commitments, execution.engine and execution.specification from an STE checkout (STE_REPO), and the exchange artifacts extend STE's core@1.0.0. The standalone path (import scl) has zero STE dependency, proven in a fresh interpreter by tests/test_standalone_boundary.py. Confirmed by code.

SCL publishes its measured requirements per workload (stable variable identity, missing-value semantics, measurement-noise provenance) to the acquisition layer through the requirement/capability exchange, and holds the shared serializer, fixture and proof_integrity.yaml byte-identical with that repository. Inferred from exchange artifacts and verify_pair_landed; there is no code call path between the two.

Computed results flow from SCL into STE: scl.ste_adapter.run_scl_specification returns STE's ExecutionResult at the SpecificationDispatcher runner seam, and interpret_*_result shapes evidence-classed 'computed' content that the caller hands to STE's own admission path. Confirmed by code and by the no-mock integration suite against a real STE checkout.

The invariant-register derivation binds a local clone of notations-acquisition-channel as a sibling party, checks its remote currency, and reports the register as only as current as its worst sibling; the acquisition channel is also the documented upstream of the SCOUT/evidence boundary (acquisition -> normalization -> evidence). Derivation dependence confirmed by code; data-flow dependence inferred from docs.

The invariant-register derivation reads a local SCL clone (BOUND_REPOSITORIES) and fails closed if it is unreachable or not in sync with its remote; and SCL's ste_adapter is the intended external runner for SpecificationDispatcher when C++/CUDA compute is needed. Runtime dependence is optional and plugged in from SCL's side; the derivation dependence is confirmed by code.

STE owns the core invariant set that the acquisition channel extends and pins as a submodule; ste_invariant_declaration.yaml is STE's authored answer to the acquisition layer's reconstruction request, and the derived register records which invariants DAQ owns versus extends. Confirmed by files in this repository; the acquisition channel's side of the binding is inferred from its exchange artifacts as read here.

STE declares core@1.0.0 and the ExecutionSpecification/ExecutionResult seam; SCL is bound to the register in extends_only mode, extends core@1.0.0 in its exchange artifacts, and mirrors STE's program/configuration/input dimension mapping and fault-code conventions. Confirmed by code and generated artifacts in this repository.
